providers.description: DeepJudge is an AI-powered legal knowledge search and intelligence platform for law firms and in-house legal teams, founded by ex-Google search engineers and legaltech veterans. It unifies scattered institutional knowledge across document management systems, SharePoint, HighQ, OneDrive, email, and intranets into a single governed, permission-aware search layer, then layers LLM-agnostic AI agents and workflow automation on top. Products include DeepJudge Knowledge Search, AI Workflows, Negotiation Intelligence, Multi-Document Chat, Matter & Client Overview, and SuperSearch for cross-matter analysis. The platform can be hosted in DeepJudge's cloud, the customer's cloud, or on premises, supports Model Context Protocol (MCP) for governed AI access to firm knowledge, and does not train on customer data. DeepJudge is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified.

providers.name: Kriptos
providers.description: Kriptos is an AI-driven unstructured data security platform that automatically discovers, classifies, and labels documents across endpoints, servers, and cloud storage, then feeds that business and risk context into the DLP, CASB, SIEM, EDR, and IAM tooling an organization already runs rather than replacing it. The platform spans data discovery and classification, data compliance and risk management, data access governance across Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, insider threat management with UEBA, DSPM, and AI governance covering shadow-AI monitoring for tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini. Classification results are written back as native Microsoft Purview and Google Drive labels. Founded in Ecuador and backed by Techstars, Kriptos reports more than 1.2 billion documents classified for over 150,000 users, with customers concentrated in banking, insurance, healthcare, and utilities across Latin America. Kriptos is a sales-led product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API documentation.

providers.name: Secuvy
providers.description: Secuvy is an AI data filtering and data security platform that combines data discovery, classification, data security posture management, privacy automation, and AI governance into a single product. The platform automates detection and classification of sensitive data across hybrid and multi-cloud environments and prevents regulated data from leaking into AI tools, assistants, and inference pipelines. Secuvy offers more than 250 connectors covering AWS, Azure, GCP, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, Slack, Jira, ServiceNow, Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, MongoDB, and on-premise systems like Windows File Servers, SharePoint, and NFS. Authentication options include OAuth, SAML, and API key based integration, and developers can build custom connectors against any system with a public API. Public API reference documentation was not located during research; technical detail is provided through Secuvy's sales and onboarding teams.

providers.name: Squadle
providers.description: Squadle is a food safety and operational compliance platform for multi-unit restaurant and foodservice operations. It combines IoT remote temperature monitoring (its Remote Temperature System) with digital food-safety checklists, shift management, and patented ZeroTouch technology that automates temperature logging and triggers corrective actions. The platform reports 3.3B+ completed tasks and 100M+ temperatures measured. Squadle was acquired by Crunchtime and now operates as part of the Crunchtime Operations Execution platform; the squadle.com domain redirects to crunchtime.com/squadle. No public API or developer platform is currently published.

providers.name: Visibly
providers.description: Visibly is a UK-based workforce compliance management platform that helps enterprises with large, distributed and subcontracted workforces automate their HSEQ (health, safety, environment and quality) obligations. It centralizes worker onboarding, competency and certification tracking, real-time compliance monitoring and alerts, audit and project reporting, and safety broadcast communications, with integrations into existing HR, ERP, LMS and SharePoint systems and mobile-first workflows for field workers. It is used across construction, manufacturing, FMCG, energy, public services, infrastructure and logistics by organizations including Network Rail, National Grid, EDF, Scottish Power, NHS and Danone. Backed by Creandum and Seedcamp.

providers.name: Billables Ai
providers.description: Billables AI is a San Francisco based legal technology company that builds AI-powered automatic time tracking software for lawyers, consultants, and professional services firms. Its platform passively captures billable activity as people work across the tools they already use — Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Zoom, Adobe, and the Chrome and Edge browsers — then uses AI to draft time entries, assign the correct client and matter, and write narrative descriptions, learning and adapting to each user over time. Privacy is user-controlled, with only the individual able to view or edit their own time records before they are submitted. The company is venture-backed (Series A) and was surfaced through the Wing Venture Capital portfolio.

providers.name: Enfusion
providers.description: Enfusion is a cloud-native, front-to-back investment management platform for hedge funds and asset managers, unifying portfolio management (PMS), order and execution management (OEMS), pre- and post-trade compliance, a unified IBOR/ABOR accounting book of record, and analytics on a single SaaS database. It serves over 1,000 clients across 30 countries, offers direct connectivity to 300+ liquidity sources via FIX, and maintains a 4M+ instrument security master. Enfusion was acquired by Clearwater Analytics (CWAN) in 2025; the enfusion.com domain now redirects to cwan.com, where Enfusion is offered as a product line. There is no public developer portal or open API specification: the platform API and knowledge base are gated behind the client web application and Zendesk help center. This profile was surfaced as an ICONIQ Capital portfolio lead and enriched from public marketing, support, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: GovGuard
providers.description: GovGuard is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) GovTech company building AI infrastructure for government agencies, starting with Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request automation. Its AI agents route incoming public-records requests, search across municipal archives (emails, meeting minutes, PDFs, and shared drives), flag personally identifiable information and other exempt material for redaction against the relevant state exemption codes, and draft response letters for clerk review while maintaining a complete audit trail. Agencies retain full ownership and control of all records and metadata, and GovGuard states that it does not train models on client data. The company was founded by Aditya Sabharwal and Gleb Hulting and is based in San Francisco.

providers.name: Jetstream
providers.description: Jetstream (jetstream.security) is a security-first AI governance platform for enterprises, backed by Redpoint Ventures. It helps organizations discover, control, and monitor AI systems at scale across five capabilities: AI Visibility (discovering and inventorying AI agents, models, tools, and workflows across environments), AI Design Control (documenting how agentic systems are assembled), Agentic Identity (binding human and AI identities to responsible owners), Runtime Governance (enforcing real-time behavioral compliance against approved designs), and AI FinOps Accountability (tracking usage and spend by model, agent, and workflow). The company positions governance as an accelerator for AI adoption, addressing shadow AI, cost control, accountability, and compliance. No public API, SDK, CLI, or developer portal is published as of this profile; the company pursues SOC 2, FedRAMP High, and DoD IL5 compliance.

providers.name: LegalZoom
providers.description: LegalZoom.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: LZ) is a Glendale, California online legal technology and services company that helps individuals and small businesses create legal documents and form, run, and grow their businesses without necessarily hiring an attorney. Founded in 1999, LegalZoom offers business formation services (LLC, S-Corp, C-Corp, nonprofit, DBA), registered agent service, EIN/tax ID filing, annual report and compliance filings, business licenses, virtual mail, business banking partnerships, trademark registration, and ongoing bookkeeping and tax services through LZ Books and LZ Tax. On the personal side it provides wills, living trusts, power of attorney, prenuptial agreements, and a partner-driven divorce flow via Divorce.com. Customers access an attorney-network legal advice subscription (LZ Legal Services / business advisory plans) connecting them to independent attorneys for consultations and document review. LegalZoom went public on Nasdaq in 2021 (ticker LZ) and serves customers primarily in the United States. The company's revenue model is transactional document and formation fees plus recurring subscription services (registered agent, compliance, attorney advice, bookkeeping). LegalZoom does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; partner integrations (e.g. divorce.com, banking partners, accounting partners) appear to be private commercial arrangements rather than self-service developer APIs. The legalzoom.com web app calls a set of internal hosts under apigw.legalzoom.com (checkout-graphql-public-api, customer, experimentation, revv, attorney-state-service, site-search) but these are first-party and not documented for third-party use.

providers.name: Opti
providers.description: Opti is an AI-native identity and access management (IAM) platform for enterprises struggling with access sprawl across human, non-human, and agentic identities. Founded in 2024 by Barak Perelman, Mille Gandelsman, and Ido Trivizki, Opti deploys pre-trained, domain-specific large language models trained on curated identity data to interpret risk, recommend least-privilege access decisions, and orchestrate safe permissions. The platform spans Access Intelligence, Risk Mitigation, Lifecycle Management (joiner/mover/leaver), and Compliance, integrating with 250+ identity solutions, IdPs, IGAs, HRIS, and ITSM systems without rip-and-replace. Opti raised a $20M seed round led by YL Ventures, Mayfield Fund, and Hetz Ventures.

providers.name: SurePath AI
providers.description: SurePath AI (now part of F5) is an enterprise AI governance and security platform that lets organizations safely adopt generative AI across their workforce. The platform gives security and IT teams visibility into GenAI usage by recording conversations, mitigates risk by detecting and redacting sensitive data in prompts and enforcing role-based access guardrails to public and private models, and increases safe adoption through a branded enterprise GenAI portal that enriches interactions with enterprise data. It is delivered as a SaaS product with an admin console rather than a public developer API, and maintains SOC 2 compliance.

providers.name: Trust & Will
providers.description: Trust & Will is a digital estate planning platform, headquartered in San Diego, California and founded in 2017, that lets individuals and families create legally valid, state-specific estate planning documents entirely online. Members build will-based or trust-based estate plans and related documents such as guardianship designations, powers of attorney, and advance healthcare directives, and the company also offers probate support and nationwide notarization. Trust & Will distributes through direct-to-consumer subscriptions as well as B2B partnerships with financial advisors, wealth managers, and employers offering it as a benefit. The platform is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; this enrichment pass found no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, but did confirm a live security program and trust posture.

providers.name: doinstruct
providers.description: doinstruct is an AI-powered frontline training and compliance platform for deskless and shift-based workforces. Founded in Osnabrück, Germany in 2021 and now headquartered in Brooklyn, New York with an office in Berlin, it turns internal SOPs, documents, and expert knowledge into mobile-first courses delivered in 35+ languages. Its Genius AI authoring tool, a 400+ lesson training library, a manager dashboard for assigning and documenting training, and a mobile learner experience serve 400+ frontline teams across food & beverage, logistics, manufacturing, construction, and general compliance, with audit-ready reporting for standards such as HACCP, GFSI, and ISO 27001. Backed by Creandum and HV Capital.

providers.name: exein
providers.description: Exein is a Physical AI and embedded/IoT cybersecurity company (Italy) that secures connected devices, firmware, and Linux/RTOS embedded systems. Its platform pairs on-device runtime threat detection (Exein Runtime) with AI-powered firmware analysis and SBOM ingestion (Exein Analyzer), mapping findings to standards including the EU Cyber Resilience Act, ETSI EN 303-645, IEC 62443, RED 3.3, and the US Cyber Trust Mark. Exein does not publish a hosted public REST API; its developer surface is open-source security tooling in the exein-io GitHub organization — notably Pulsar (an eBPF-powered runtime security agent) and Kepler (a NIST-based CVE lookup store and API). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital, hv-capital, and partech.

providers.name: Vector Solutions
providers.description: Vector Solutions is a SaaS provider of industry-specific training, operational readiness, workforce management, and risk-management software. Its portfolio spans Learning Management Systems (LMS), Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) management, staff scheduling, incident and equipment tracking, professional development and evaluation management, and large online course libraries. The company serves education (K-12 and higher ed), public safety (fire, EMS, law enforcement), government, manufacturing, construction, and gaming markets, helping organizations prepare their people, stay in compliance, and manage operational risk. Vector Solutions is a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It runs a GraphQL endpoint at api.vectorsolutions.com/graphql that backs its applications; that endpoint is live but not publicly documented and has schema introspection disabled.

providers.name: Ellis
providers.description: Ellis is a modern business immigration platform and law firm that helps company People and HR teams secure U.S. work visas and green cards for skilled talent. The platform combines licensed immigration attorneys with software for centralized case management, document storage, status tracking, and program analytics, covering employment-based visas (H-1B, TN, O-1, L-1, J-1, E-1/E-2, E-3), green cards (EB-1A, EB-2 NIW, EB-2/EB-3 PERM), and naturalization. Ellis is a Kindred Ventures portfolio company. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public web surface; Ellis publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable artifacts at this time.

providers.name: Eudia
providers.description: Eudia is an enterprise augmented-intelligence platform for in-house legal, compliance, and procurement teams at large organizations and government agencies. Its "Enterprise Brain" ingests a company's contracts, policies, precedents, and prior decisions and codifies the judgment of its legal experts into governed AI workflows, while "Expert Digital Twins" let business teams self-serve governed legal guidance without direct attorney involvement. Products span compliance automation, contracting, decision self-service, mergers and acquisitions, and litigation support, with connectors into Microsoft, Google Drive, SharePoint, Box, Salesforce, DocuSign, OnIt, and LinkSquares. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Eudia raised a Series A of up to $105M led by General Catalyst with Sierra Ventures, Floodgate, and Defy Partners. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, trust, and security posture.

providers.name: Eunice
providers.description: Eunice is a London-based AI fintech building institutional-grade due diligence and monitoring infrastructure for digital assets and private markets. Its platform automates token due diligence, classification, risk analysis, and disclosure requirements — including an AI-powered MiCA whitepaper library for streamlining compliance with the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation — and delivers insights through a dashboard and API to exchanges, funds, custodians, issuers, and regulators. Founded in 2021 by Yi Luo, a second-time fintech entrepreneur and former VC, Eunice raised $8M in combined Seed and Pre-Seed funding led by Moonfire Ventures and Speedinvest with participation from Openspace Ventures in 2026, and counts Coinbase, Crypto.com, Copper, and Zodia Custody among its clients.

providers.name: Geocomply
providers.description: GeoComply is a geolocation compliance, digital identity, and fraud-prevention company that provides the location-verification and anti-fraud intelligence layer behind many of the world's most regulated digital platforms. Its product suite spans GeoComply Core (location-based fraud detection and geolocation compliance), IDComply (KYC and AML identity verification), GeoGuard (VPN and proxy/spoofing detection), PinPoint (on-property geofencing), the Chargeback Integrator (GCI), and the OneComply licensing-management platform, serving the iGaming, financial services, media/entertainment, and cryptocurrency industries. GeoComply's integrations are enterprise, sales-led engagements rather than a public self-serve developer portal; this profile was surfaced as a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company and has been enriched from GeoComply's public security, trust, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Agentero
providers.description: Agentero is a digital insurance network and insurtech platform, founded in 2017 and based in Oakland, California, that gives independent property & casualty insurance agents market access to 100+ national and regional carriers alongside modern agency technology. Its unified command center lets agents get appointed, quote and bind policies, manage carrier appointments, and reconcile commissions from a single portal, with no startup fees or minimum-volume requirements. Agentero also offers an AI Appetite Checker that matches risks to the right carriers and Producerflow, a compliance and producer-management solution for carriers, MGAs, and agencies. Agentero is a portfolio company backed by Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Corvus (Travelers)
providers.description: Corvus by Travelers is a cyber-insurance provider offering Smart Cyber Insurance and Smart Tech E&O coverage alongside data-driven cyber risk management. Now part of Travelers, Corvus underwrites cyber policies using threat intelligence and AI-driven data, and pairs coverage with continuous threat monitoring, vulnerability detection, a cyber risk dashboard, and 24/7 incident response and claims support. The business is broker-focused, distributing through appointed brokers via its Broker Hub and broker sign-in portal. Corvus was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Cowbell Cyber
providers.description: Cowbell is a cyber insurance provider (insurtech) that delivers adaptive, continuously-underwritten cyber liability coverage and cyber-risk management services to small businesses and the middle market. Its platform pairs insurance products with proprietary risk analytics — Cowbell Factors, a continuous risk-rating model that benchmarks an organization's exposure against peers — and closed-loop resilience services delivered through the Cowbell console for policyholders, agents, and brokers. Product lines include Cowbell Prime 100 / Prime 100 Pro (small business), Prime 250 / Prime One (middle market), Prime Plus (excess), Technology Errors & Omissions, Management Liability, plus the Cowbell Rx marketplace, Cowbell Connectors, and Cowbell Insights. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Cowbell publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal — the console at console.cowbellcyber.ai is an authenticated quoting/policy application for agents and insureds, not a documented programmatic API.

providers.name: Fable
providers.description: Fable Security is an AI-powered human risk management (HRM) platform that helps security teams reduce incidents by changing employee behavior. It combines behavioral interventions (targeted nudges and AI-generated content), phishing simulations, short-form video awareness briefings, and human-risk reporting into a single platform positioned as a modern replacement for legacy security-awareness training. Fable's AI Studio, Composer, and Briefing Agent generate custom video and audio content - including deepfake and voice-fake simulations - and produce audience-targeted briefings from emerging threats in minutes. The platform reports on human risk and compliance across the workforce and integrates with an organization's identity framework, workspace, and security tooling. Fable serves healthcare, financial services, and technology customers including Sisense, SanDisk, Red Hat, PennyMac, Genesys, and Dayton Children's Hospital, and is backed by Greylock and Techstars.

providers.name: MedThread
providers.description: MedThread is an AI-powered Health Information Management (HIM) platform built specifically for long-term and post-acute care facilities — skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), nursing homes, assisted living facilities (ALFs), and rehabilitation centers. The platform digitizes paper records with AI-powered scanning, runs continuous automated audits for documentation completeness and regulatory compliance, monitors CMS quality metrics (rehospitalization, pressure ulcers, antipsychotic use), and provides a compliance dashboard, provider portal, and patient-facing Personal Health Record (PHR). MedThread advertises FHIR compatibility and pre-built EHR integrations (Epic, Cerner, Allscripts, eClinicalWorks, NextGen, Meditech, athenahealth, Greenway, Practice Fusion) via a secure API. Techstars-backed and based in Miami, FL. No public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Newfront Insurance
providers.description: Newfront is a technology-native insurance brokerage ("a brokerage for the 21st century") serving startups through Fortune 500 enterprises, and now part of WTW. It places business insurance (property, casualty, cyber, executive risk, workers' compensation, surety, aviation, M&A and global programs) alongside Total Rewards services (employee benefits, compensation, retirement/401(k), HR, payroll and benefits compliance), pairing brokerage expertise with in-house software such as the Navigator benefits platform, RiskPulse analytics, and contract/coverage-gap review tools. Newfront reports roughly 20% of U.S. unicorns as clients and $3.1B in annual premiums placed. The company exposes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or webhooks; client and employee interaction happens through the authenticated app.newfront.com application. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched with company identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Vouch
providers.description: Vouch is a San Francisco, California business insurance broker and risk advisor purpose-built for high-growth startups and the venture ecosystem. Founded in 2018 by Sam Hodges and Travis Hedge and backed by investors including Ribbit Capital, SVB Capital, Redpoint Ventures, Y Combinator, and MS&AD Ventures, Vouch offers a tailored portfolio of commercial coverages — Directors & Officers (D&O), Errors & Omissions (E&O / Tech E&O / Professional Services E&O), Cyber, Employment Practices Liability (EPL), General Liability, Business Property, Fiduciary, Crime, and contract-required coverages — sold to technology, healthcare and life sciences, financial services, and professional services companies. The business model is broker-of-record commissions and, since 2021, a Vouch-owned insurance carrier underwriting select lines. Vouch is best known in the developer community for its embedded insurance program, which lets ecosystem partners (Carta, StartupOS, and similar founder platforms) pre-fill applications, surface quotes, and bind coverage inline via Vouch's partner API. Public developer documentation, an OpenAPI specification, and a self-serve sandbox are not exposed; the partner API and Vouch Corporate documentation (hosted on GitBook) are gated to onboarded venture, technology, and service-provider partners contracted through hello@vouch.us.

providers.name: rekord
providers.description: Rekord is a Dublin-based fintech platform that helps banks and fintechs automate credit underwriting and customer onboarding. Its AI-native decisioning platform unifies data from many sources into a single view, orchestrates decision workflows, runs a natural-language policy engine, and provides AI-assisted case management so credit and risk teams can make defensible, transparent decisions at scale. Rekord surfaces the signal buried in large volumes of applicant and transaction data to speed underwriting and onboarding while enforcing identity verification and compliance. It is a portfolio company of point-nine. Rekord does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine discovery surface; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Icertis
providers.description: Icertis is an AI-native contract intelligence company that turns enterprise contracts into structured, actionable data and measurable business outcomes. Its Contract Intelligence (ICI) platform manages agreements across their full lifecycle — authoring, negotiation, execution, obligation management, and ongoing analytics — spanning sell-side, buy-side, and corporate contracts. The platform pairs a configurable contract data model with AI capabilities (the "Vera" AI assistant and agent-powered drafting, redlining, and negotiation) trained on millions of contracts. Icertis serves large enterprises across manufacturing, life sciences, healthcare, technology, financial services, and the public sector, and integrates with ERP, CRM, CPQ, and procurement systems such as SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, and Coupa. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched from Icertis' public web presence.

providers.name: Ipid
providers.description: iPiD (International Payments Identity) is a fintech providing real-time Know Your Payee (KYP) verification for cross-border and domestic payments. Its single, payment-rail-agnostic API lets banks, PSPs, and corporates validate bank account ownership and match payee names before funds move, reducing authorized push payment (APP) fraud, business email compromise losses, and failed transactions. Products include iPiD Validate (global payee / bank account verification with name-matching), iPiD Node (a scheme-compliance layer for EU Verification of Payee, UK Confirmation of Payee, FATF Recommendation 16, and US Nacha), and a Payment Agent agentic verification layer. Founded in 2021, iPiD is backed by QED Investors, Monk's Hill Ventures, Quona Capital, Jungle Ventures, Saison Capital, and others. Public API access is gated behind a sales/demo process; no machine-readable specification is published publicly.

providers.name: LedgiFi
providers.description: LedgiFi (formerly Krypto Ledgers) is a Latin American cryptocurrency tax and portfolio-tracking platform founded in 2020 and headquartered in Antofagasta, Chile. The product syncs a user's transaction history from exchanges and wallets — Binance, Coinbase, Kraken and MetaMask among them — normalizes it across more than 25,000 assets, and computes realized capital gains using the valuation methods and monetary-correction adjustments each jurisdiction requires, so investors can file a compliant return. Its Chilean profile applies the SII's specific rules (IPC indexation and dollar-variation adjustments, Impuesto de Primera Categoría and Impuesto Global Complementario), and the platform has since expanded to Mexico, Spain, Colombia and Argentina. Alongside tax reporting it offers a portfolio view spanning crypto, stocks and ETFs, with per-asset performance and allocation. LedgiFi is a 500 Global (500 LatAm B18) portfolio company. It runs a monitored production API at api.ledgifi.com that backs its own web and mobile apps, but publishes no developer portal, no API specification and no self-service API program.

providers.name: Periphery
providers.description: Periphery is a cybersecurity company providing embedded, device-level threat management for critical industrial and defence platforms. Its lightweight, architecture-agnostic agent secures, fingerprints, and continuously monitors devices, detecting unauthorized changes and hardening what is risky even in constrained, offline, or air-gapped environments. The platform spans three products: Insights (point-in-time security evaluation with agent-based pen-testing and SBOM risk analysis), Vantage (on-prem intelligence that establishes a known-good baseline, detects change, and restores devices), and Outpost (real-time on-device threat detection and prevention for air-gapped deployments). Periphery targets regulatory compliance across NDAA, EU CRA, NIS2, UN R155, UN R156, and IEC 62443. It is a Techstars portfolio company.

providers.name: Xayn (now Noxtua)
providers.description: Xayn is a Berlin-based AI company founded in 2017 as XAIN out of research by Dr. Leif-Nissen Lundbaek and Prof. Michael Huth at Oxford and Imperial College London. Rebranded to Xayn in 2020, it built the Xaynet privacy-preserving federated learning framework and a privacy-protecting search and discovery engine. In February 2024 the company pivoted to legal AI and rebranded as Noxtua AG (noxtua.com), Europe's sovereign Legal AI for research, document analysis, and drafting, backed by a Series A of EUR 10M (2021, Global Brain/KDDI, with Earlybird) and a Series B of roughly EUR 81M led by legal publisher C.H. Beck. xayn.com is offline and the company publishes no public API or developer portal today; its former open-source SDKs and packages are archived.

providers.name: District Cover
providers.description: District Cover is a commercial insurance managing general agent and surplus-lines broker focused on urban businesses. It underwrites flexible commercial coverage for city-based retailers, restaurants, bakeries, laundromats, dry cleaners, salons, law and medical offices, and multi-location mid-market operators, using block-level risk scoring drawn from crime and fire analytics rather than broad ZIP-code assessments. The platform supports real-time submissions, multi-location quoting, and property-only endorsements, and is distributed to brokers through a licensed producer network operating across multiple U.S. states. District Cover publishes no public API or developer program; broker access is delivered through a hosted Insly portal.

providers.name: imgauth — API di attestazione opere digitali
providers.description: Digital-work attestation and proof-of-existence service by Spazio Genesi ETS. Clients compute a SHA-256 fingerprint locally (file bytes never leave the device) and receive a signed PDF certificate, an RFC 3161 timestamp, and an OpenTimestamps/Bitcoin anchor. Exposes a public REST API (OpenAPI 3.0.3) and a hosted remote MCP server for agents.

providers.name: Ajax
providers.description: Ajax is an AI-powered timekeeping platform built specifically for law firms. It automatically captures attorney work across applications, documents, emails, phone calls, and video meetings, then generates OCG-compliant, voice-matched time-entry narratives and syncs them with one click to practice-management and billing systems. Ajax integrates with SurePoint, Clio, MyCase, Filevine, PracticePanther, Centerbase, Actionstep, and Soluno, and positions itself around recovering otherwise-lost billable hours. The company is SOC 2 aligned, encrypts data in transit and at rest, does not train models on customer data, and enforces rolling data deletion. Ajax is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a product/SaaS company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Certivity
providers.description: Certivity is a Munich-based RegTech company, founded in 2021, that operates an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform for regulated industries such as automotive, aerospace, and connected vehicles. Its product, Certivity Core, turns complex regulations, standards, and internal documents into structured, machine-readable, engineering-ready requirements with full traceability and real-time monitoring of legal changes across 50+ jurisdictions. The platform digitizes and structures regulatory content from publishers such as ISO, IEC, CEN, CENELEC, ASTM, UL, and SAE using a proprietary ingestion pipeline and a regulatory knowledge graph, and integrates directly into engineering workflows (including Jama Connect) via an official API. Backed by Earlybird, High-Tech Gruenderfonds, UVC Partners, and Almaz Capital, Certivity added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Greenplaces
providers.description: Greenplaces is a sustainability and ESG reporting platform that pairs software with expert consulting to help companies — especially suppliers responding to enterprise requirements — measure their carbon footprint under the GHG Protocol and complete sustainability framework submissions including CDP, EcoVadis, SBTi, GRI, SASB/ISSB and GRESB. The managed-service platform also supports B Corp certification, CSRD readiness, SOC 2 and AI-governance compliance, and tracking of regulations such as California SB 253 and SB 261. Greenplaces is venture-backed by Felicis and Redpoint Ventures. Added to the API Evangelist network from VC portfolio data; the company publishes a managed product (app.greenplaces.com) but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Lightbeam
providers.description: Lightbeam is an AI data security and guardrails platform that discovers and classifies sensitive data across cloud, SaaS and on-premises systems, ties that data to identity and access context through its Data Identity Graph, and enforces guardrails on how users, applications, copilots and AI agents reach it. Capabilities span AI security and shadow-AI detection, data security posture management (DSPM), data classification, risk scoring, automated remediation, access governance, privacy operations, data retention, breach and ransomware blast-radius reduction, and user entity behavior analytics. Founded by former Nutanix leaders and backed by Vertex Ventures US, 8VC, Village Global, Monta Vista Capital and Dropbox. Lightbeam sells to the enterprise and publishes no public API - its documentation portal is authentication-gated.

providers.name: kWh Analytics
providers.description: kWh Analytics is a Beaverton, Oregon based managing general agent and data-analytics firm that underwrites property and performance insurance for renewable energy assets — solar, wind, and battery storage. Founded in 2012 and acquired by specialist insurer Beazley in 2023, the company operates what it describes as the industry's largest solar performance database, covering roughly 30% of U.S. solar assets across 300,000+ renewable energy assets and $100B+ in loss data. Its HelioStats platform ingests unstructured asset production documents (via AWS S3, Box, Dropbox, email attachment, or API) and applies OCR and machine learning to extract, validate, standardize, benchmark, and enrich operating data for investors, lenders, and asset owners. Commercial products include data-driven Property Insurance, the Solar Revenue Put credit enhancement, the Wind Proxy Hedge, and the SolarScape market intelligence offering. kWh Analytics also publishes the annual Solar Risk Assessment industry report. There is no public developer portal, published API reference, or machine-readable API specification — data delivery and the HelioStats ingest API are arranged through enterprise engagement.

providers.name: Manex AI
providers.description: Manex AI (Manex AI GmbH) is a European enterprise AI company that builds Kosmos, an Autonomous Enterprise AI Platform for industrial and manufacturing OEMs and their suppliers. Kosmos models the domains a business runs on and lets AI agents, workflows, and applications act on full enterprise context instead of fragments. On top of Kosmos, Manex ships purpose-built autonomous suites: Blackbelt (computer-aided quality / CAQ), Takt (manufacturing execution / MES), and Gemba (shopfloor operations), plus Horizon, a distribution platform that makes a solution built at one site instantly available to every other. Manex serves aerospace, automotive, chemistry, electronics, semiconductors, pharma and biotech, heavy equipment, industrial machinery, and home-appliance manufacturers. Made in Europe and built for the strictest compliance standards, the platform runs in cloud, on-premise, or hybrid environments with customer-controlled data residency, GDPR options, ISO 27001 and TISAX certification, enterprise access control, and full audit history. Manex AI is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: EXIGER
providers.description: Exiger is an AI-native supply chain, third-party, and software supply chain risk and compliance company. Its 1Exiger platform unifies supplier, product, part, component, and risk data into a single system to help organizations map and orchestrate compliant, resilient physical and software supply chains. Product areas span supply chain visibility and optimization, trade and third-party risk and compliance, due diligence intelligence (DDIQ), and software supply chain security (SBOM analysis, from its Ion Channel acquisition). Exiger serves government and commercial customers and is FedRAMP authorized. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio company and enriched from Exiger's public corporate, trust, and legal surfaces; Exiger does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Grade
providers.description: Grade is the API for performance-based payroll, letting companies pay workers, creators, contractors, and AI agents based on results rather than hours worked. Companies push performance signals into Grade via webhooks or direct API calls (task completed, milestone hit, content published, views tracked, invoice processed), and Grade runs them against configurable payout rules — flat fees, tiered commissions, threshold bonuses, or blended structures — handling the math, de-duplication, and approval workflows automatically. Grade tracks every post across platforms, approves and distributes bulk payouts in one click, and handles compliance end to end: KYC verification, tax-form collection, DAC7 reporting, worker classification, and merchant-of-record services. Payouts reach 190+ countries via local bank transfers, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, Airtm, and USDT, with no separate creator account required. Grade (YC W26) is based in San Francisco and has paid out $10M+ to date.

providers.name: Storyboard
providers.description: Storyboard is a fleet-operations AI platform that gives trucking and logistics companies voice-first, hands-free AI workers for their drivers. The system automates dispatch updates, driver coaching, safety alerts, and compliance monitoring (including hours-of-service and idling) so back-office teams field fewer phone calls and drivers stay hands-free on the road. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Santa Monica, California, Storyboard began as an enterprise podcast and internal-audio communication platform (a $4.5M seed round led by CRV in 2020) before pivoting to AI-powered fleet operations. It is distributed through in-cab telematics marketplaces such as Platform Science and ISAAC Instruments. Storyboard exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; access is via its web and mobile apps at app.storyboard.com. This profile was surfaced as a CRV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Defense Contract Management Agency
providers.description: The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) is the Department of Defense component that works directly with defense suppliers to help ensure that DoD, federal, and allied government supplies and services are delivered on time, at projected cost, and meet performance requirements. DCMA performs contract administration, quality assurance, and earned value management oversight, but does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Hokan
providers.description: Hokan, Inc. (株式会社hokan) is a Japanese InsurTech company that builds hokan®, a cloud-based customer and contract management (CRM) system for insurance agencies and brokerages. The platform consolidates customer and policy information, digitizes proposal and activity workflows, and adds modules for intent capture (意向把握), case management (案件管理), dashboards, accounting/cashiering (出納), and staff management (People). It targets paperless operations, stronger audit and compliance controls, renewal and aftercare tracking, and mobile access for agents. Customers include Orix Life, ANA, Sekisui, and other Japanese insurers and agencies. Hokan is backed by 500 Global. The company exposes API-based website integration for its product but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: SarisAI
providers.description: SarisAI (Saris) builds agentic AI workflow automation for banks and credit unions, automating multi-step back-office operations across lending, compliance, and operations while keeping human oversight and audit trails. Its platform runs six specialized AI agents (Document, System, Inbox, Audit & Monitoring, External, and Income & Financial Analysis) that handle document intake, income verification, data validation, borrower communication, and post-close regulatory checks across mortgage, consumer, and commercial lending. Saris integrates directly with core banking, loan origination, and document systems (Fiserv, Encompass, OnBase/Hyland, Meridian) and LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini). The company is a Homebrew-backed fintech and is SOC 2, GDPR, GLBA, and CUSO certified. It is a private B2B platform with no public developer API, OpenAPI, or self-service surface; this profile captures its identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Syndio
providers.description: Syndio is an enterprise workplace-equity and compensation-governance software company. Its AI-assisted platform helps large organizations make defensible, compliant pay decisions at scale, spanning offers, promotions, merit cycles, and pay-equity/pay-transparency compliance (including EU Pay Transparency Directive requirements). The platform is organized into Essentials (foundations for aligned, compliant pay decisions), Decisions (real-time guidance during pay decision-making), and Predict (forward-looking workforce intelligence), all powered by the domain-specific Syndi AI. Syndio reports governing more than $1T in pay decisions for 350+ global enterprises. It is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS accessed via the app with OAuth 2 / SSO; there is no public self-serve developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI definition. First-party developer-facing surfaces are limited to the syndioctl command-line tool and a public GitHub organization. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Threat Stack
providers.description: Threat Stack was a Boston-based cloud security company providing full-stack cloud security observability, intrusion detection, and compliance monitoring for infrastructure and applications across cloud-native workloads including virtual machines, containers, and Kubernetes. Its platform combined rules and supervised machine learning to detect threats, vulnerabilities, and attacks in real time. Threat Stack exposed a RESTful V2 API (HAWK/HMAC authenticated) and trigger-based webhook alerts, along with first-party SDKs, a Go CLI, and configuration-management modules (Chef, Ansible, Puppet, Terraform, CloudFormation, Helm). The company was acquired by F5 in 2021 and the product is now F5 Distributed Cloud App Infrastructure Protection (AIP); the original threatstack.com and api.threatstack.com domains have been decommissioned.

providers.name: Pylon (formerly Braid Lending)
providers.description: Pylon (formerly Braid Lending) is an AI-native mortgage infrastructure company founded in 2022 and headquartered in New York, New York, backed by investors including 500 Global and Citi. Pylon operates as "America's mortgage rails," an API-first, MCP-native platform that lets brokers, fintechs, lenders, and banks build and automate mortgage origination end to end — from application through underwriting, decisioning, compliance, and capital markets settlement. Every aspect of mortgage fulfillment is powered by APIs, complemented by a white-label "Elements" UI component library for embedding fully digital, autonomous mortgage experiences. The public developer surface (API reference, integration guides, and a live playground) is gated behind a developer-access request form, so no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted docs were discoverable during enrichment.

providers.name: UL Solutions
providers.description: UL Solutions is a global leader in applied safety science, providing testing, inspection, certification, advisory, and software solutions to help customers innovate safely, demonstrate compliance, and bring trusted products to market. The company offers software products such as ULTRUS and ComplianceWire, customer portals (myUL, Product iQ), and the Marks and Labels Hub. UL Solutions does not currently expose a public developer-facing API portal with open documentation.

providers.name: Wexler
providers.description: Wexler AI operates a Fact Intelligence Platform built for legal disputes and investigations. Its AI system, including an assistant named Kim, extracts, structures, and verifies facts across large document sets with source attribution, surfaces inconsistencies and contradictions in evidence, builds chronological case timelines, and produces confidence-scored, testable facts grounded in source materials. It is used by enterprise and AmLaw100 law firms for early case assessment. Wexler currently exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Monitaur
providers.description: Monitaur is an enterprise AI governance platform that helps regulated organizations manage machine learning and AI responsibly across the full model lifecycle. Its software lets teams define enterprise-wide AI governance policies, manage and monitor model performance for drift and bias, and automate model validation, risk assessment, stress testing, and vendor governance at scale. Monitaur is built for regulated industries such as insurance and financial services, delivering audit-ready documentation and compliance reporting. A Techstars-backed company, Monitaur has been recognized as a Gartner Magic Quadrant Visionary and is SOC 2 Type II certified. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Responsiv
providers.description: Responsiv is an AI-powered regulatory intelligence and compliance platform that helps organizations monitor regulatory change, translate laws and regulations into clear actionable requirements, identify compliance gaps against existing policies and controls, and track remediation through to completion. The platform continuously monitors 1,000+ regulatory sources across 50+ jurisdictions, routes alerts by business unit, topic, or jurisdiction, maintains an obligations register, and offers agentic legal research with fully cited sources. It serves compliance teams in financial services, health and P&C insurance, and consumer tech. Backed by Greylock. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Talk-A-Bot
providers.description: Talk-A-Bot is a Budapest-based, Techstars-backed enterprise chatbot company building compliance-first conversational AI for regulated industries including banking, healthcare, government, retail, and HR. Its platform emphasizes "zero hallucination" answers grounded only in verified knowledge bases, full conversation logging and audit trails, EU-based infrastructure with on-premise deployment options, and daily human review. Products include an FAQ Chatbot, an Agentic Chatbot, FeedbackHub, and the CHEQ internal-communications assistant, deployed across web, mobile, Messenger, and Viber. The company markets an API-first architecture for integrating with customer systems (CRM, ERP, payments, ticketing, HR) but publishes no public self-serve developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK; engagement is full-service. Compliance posture spans HIPAA, DORA, the EU AI Act, GDPR, and PCI DSS.

providers.name: Withcoverage
providers.description: WithCoverage is a technology-driven risk management and commercial insurance platform that aims to replace the traditional insurance broker for growing businesses. It pairs a team of insurance advisors, claims specialists, and attorneys with an AI-powered digital platform to analyze policies, reduce premiums, manage certificates of insurance, and handle claims proactively as companies scale. Headquartered in New York City and backed by venture investors including 8vc, WithCoverage operates in the insurtech sector. This API Evangelist profile was created as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline; the company currently exposes no public developer API surface (client access is through the app.withcoverage.com web application).

providers.name: Adalah for IT Systems LLC
providers.description: Adalah for IT Systems LLC operates Qanoniah, a Saudi Arabian legal technology platform that enables companies to access, understand, and act on the latest and most accurate legal information and procedures in seconds. The AI-driven service targets legal and compliance teams across Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been discovered to date.

providers.name: Aletiq
providers.description: Aletiq is a French software company building a next-generation, AI-powered Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Product Data Management (PDM) platform for regulated manufacturers. The platform centralizes technical data (CAD files, drawings, bills of materials, configurations, and work instructions), enforces traceability and regulatory compliance, and automates business processes such as approvals, engineering change management, and project milestones. Aletiq emphasizes rapid deployment and high adoption across operational teams, and integrates with major CAD tools (SolidWorks, CATIA, Autodesk Inventor, Siemens NX, Creo) and ERP systems (SAP, Sage, Cegid, Infor, Odoo) via connectors and a custom-integration API. It serves aerospace and defense, medical devices, energy, electronics, automotive, and luxury-goods industries. Aletiq is backed by Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile.

providers.name: AWST
providers.description: AWST is the software company behind WorkRamen, a productivity and business-operations platform aimed at small and medium businesses, startups, agencies, and freelancers. WorkRamen brings meeting scheduling (with Google Calendar and Outlook sync, plus Google Meet and Zoom), trackable document sharing, secure e-signatures, routing forms, visitor management, and Stripe-based payment acceptance into a single workspace. AWST is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a SaaS product only — its brand domain awst.io redirects to workramen.com, and no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or API documentation surface could be found.

providers.name: Con.doit
providers.description: Con.doit (condoit.io) is a digital platform for electrical contractors that turns field-captured electrical infrastructure data into recurring service revenue. Its mobile capture app collects on-site photos, thermal scans, and system data, then generates same-day infrared thermography reports, auto-updating single-line diagrams, asset tags, arc flash studies, and NFPA 70B preventive-maintenance programs. Con.doit is a FLIR Global Approved App and reports over 4.5 million electrical assets under management across 2,000+ critical facilities nationwide. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification is currently published; this profile is enriched from the public marketing surface only.

providers.name: Cowbell
providers.description: Cowbell is a Pleasanton, California-based adaptive cyber insurance provider serving small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) and the middle market with standalone cyber liability coverage, technology errors & omissions (Tech E&O), management liability, and excess cyber products. Founded in 2019, Cowbell pioneered continuous underwriting through its proprietary Cowbell Factors risk benchmarking, which scores organizations against millions of data points to surface vulnerabilities and prioritize remediation. The company pairs its policies with a closed-loop resiliency program (assess-insure-respond-improve) that includes complimentary risk assessments, Cowbell Insights threat detection, incident response planning, cybersecurity awareness training, micro-penetration testing, and vendor risk assessments, plus subscription-based managed detection and response (MDR), penetration testing, identity monitoring (IdentityAI), and Compliance-as-a-Service (COMPaaS). Cowbell operates across the United States (all 50 states plus DC), the United Kingdom, and Australia, is backed by reinsurance partners including Zurich, and offers a public developer program at developers.cowbellcyber.ai exposing REST APIs for agencies, accounts, risk factors, quoting, binding, policy management, and webhooks across its Prime 100, Prime 250, and PrimeOne products. The API surface powers digital aggregator integrations with partners such as Bold Penguin, Herald, Semsee, Sayata, Limit, iBynd, and AmWins. No public OpenAPI specification or open-source SDK is published by Cowbell.

providers.name: HeavyConnect
providers.description: HeavyConnect is a digital documentation and compliance platform purpose-built for agricultural operations, serving growers, harvesters, shippers, and processors. Its mobile-first, offline-capable modules cover food safety compliance, worker training and certification, time and productivity tracking, quality assurance inspections, end-to-end traceability, and supplier management. The platform replaces paper-based recordkeeping with audit-ready digital documentation and real-time analytics dashboards, helping food and agriculture operations stay inspection-ready. HeavyConnect reports 2,600+ active users across operations including Sysco, Naturipe, Talley, and Empire. It is offered as a month-to-month subscription with a request-a-demo onboarding path. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio-company lead (500 Global, Techstars) and enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Novee Security
providers.description: Novee Security (Novee) is a cybersecurity company delivering AI-driven penetration testing that finds vulnerabilities faster, validates defenses, and reduces cyber risk. Its autonomous offensive-security platform performs penetration testing at machine speed across web applications and APIs, and spans solutions including DAST, AI red teaming, manual penetration testing, bug bounty, and compliance testing. Backed by Canaan Partners, Novee is building continuous, AI-native security testing as an alternative to traditional DAST scanning and slow, periodic manual pentest cycles. The company publishes a marketing and product site, a vulnerability glossary, and a blog, but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Paladin
providers.description: Paladin is a legal technology company whose software platform connects the pro bono community and empowers legal teams to run pro bono programs more efficiently. The platform provides centralized program management dashboards, volunteer matching that connects attorneys to pro bono opportunities based on interest and expertise, and impact measurement that visualizes and reports on program outcomes across a nationwide network of legal services organizations, law firms, in-house legal teams, law schools, and bar associations. Customers include Clifford Chance, Dentons, Holland & Knight, and Wilson Sonsini. Paladin is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes a customer-facing web application at app.joinpaladin.com but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: Prolaera
providers.description: Prolaera is a learning and compliance platform built for modern CPAs and accounting firms, combining automated CPE (Continuing Professional Education) tracking, a learning management system (LMS), and a built-in course library so firms can administer training, monitor license and compliance requirements, and manage professional development in one place. Prolaera merged with LCvista and now operates as "Prolaera by LCvista"; the product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application at app.prolaera.com with SSO/SAML 2.0 identity support and SCORM/AICC/xAPI content compatibility. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Prolaera does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Seso
providers.description: Seso is an all-in-one employee management platform built for U.S. agricultural operations, serving customers across all 50 states including 35 of the top 100 agricultural employers. Its software combines a modern farm HR system, compliant digital onboarding (I-9/W-4 with direct E-Verify integration), H-2A visa filing and compliance backed by legal resources, self-serve and managed payroll, and digital paycards for paycheck delivery. Seso also provides H-2A worker services such as consulate scheduling, recruiting, and logistics coordinated from its Monterrey, Mexico office. Backed by Bond Capital and Index Ventures. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Tenkara
providers.description: Tenkara is an AI-powered operations and supply chain platform for material manufacturers across food, supplements, cosmetics, chemicals, beverages, and OTC products. The platform automates 75+ workflows spanning supplier sourcing and qualification, procurement, freight and logistics booking, order tracking, and compliance documentation (COA, SDS, and audit records), helping manufacturers find better suppliers faster, prevent delays, and run more efficient operations. Tenkara is backed by True Ventures.

providers.name: TriNet
providers.description: TriNet is a Dublin, California-based professional employer organization (PEO) for small and mid-market businesses, founded in 1988 by Martin Babinec and led today by President and CEO Mike Simonds. TriNet delivers full-service HR through a co-employment model — payroll processing, Fortune-500-grade health, retirement and ancillary benefits, workers' compensation, employment-practices liability coverage, compliance and risk management, and strategic HR advisory — to thousands of SMBs across the United States. The company offers two main packages: TriNet PEO (full co-employment) and HR Plus (technology platform plus support). TriNet is publicly traded on the NYSE as TNET with trailing-twelve-month revenue of roughly $5.0B as of FY2025. TriNet exposes its HR Customer Platform through three SwaggerHub-documented API groups — DCP, HRIS, and PEO — covering Employees, Companies, Payroll, Money, and Time-Off domains, with API credentials issued to approved customers and Integration Center partners rather than offered as a fully open developer program; OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman/Insomnia collections, a sandbox, OAuth playground, and webhook management are available to authorized developers. Public 1:1 API access typically requires partner-program qualification and technical review, which is why most TriNet customers consume the platform via the curated Integration Center marketplace (accounting, HRIS, identity, ATS, payroll, benefits and learning partners) or via unified-API aggregators such as Finch, Merge, Apideck and Truto.

providers.name: Verbal
providers.description: Verbal (tryverbal.com) is an AI-powered clinical compliance and quality-assurance platform for healthcare organizations. It automatically audits patient interactions — phone and video calls, telehealth visits, AI-agent conversations, and clinical chart notes — against customizable regulatory and quality checklists, scoring compliance in real time and surfacing gaps for supervisors and QA teams. Verbal integrates with communications and EHR platforms including Zoom, Five9, Epic, and Athena. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and customer app but no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Alix
providers.description: Alix is an estate settlement service that pairs technology with human experts — Settlement Specialists, fiduciaries, CPAs, and probate attorneys — to execute the 150+ administrative, legal, financial, and tax tasks required to settle an estate after a death. It coordinates probate court filings, asset discovery (50-state unclaimed-property and federal life-insurance searches, hidden 401(k)s and bank accounts), estate bank-account and IRS EIN setup, creditor and debt negotiation, final personal (1040) and estate (1041) tax filings, property liquidation and estate sales, and the legally compliant distribution of funds to beneficiaries — while keeping the executor informed through a dedicated app. Alix charges a flat 1% of gross estate value (minimum $9,000, $2,500 initial deposit). Backed by Initialized Capital.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Arteria AI
providers.description: Arteria AI is an enterprise AI company for financial services that positions itself as the agentic backbone of financial services operations. Its platform automates document-intensive workflows across the institutional client lifecycle for tier-one global financial institutions: OTC derivatives and ISDA onboarding, prime brokerage, securities services and custody, corporate and commercial lending, trade confirmations, securities lending and repo, regulatory reporting, and post-transaction loan compliance. The platform spans four layers (data, component, agentic, and workflow), combining no-code configuration, automated document generation, intelligent extraction with zero-shot models, clause comparison and decisioning, and controlled agentic orchestration. Arteria AI is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. It does not publish a public API or developer portal; this profile captures the company identity, domain-security posture, and published compliance certifications.

providers.name: Expedock
providers.description: Expedock is a digital business process outsourcing (BPO) and document-automation company for the logistics and freight-forwarding industry. It pairs AI-powered document automation products (FCL/LCL accounts-payable automation, monthly statement automation, and commercial invoice and packing-list data entry) with tech-enabled remote teams supported by operations managers and QA specialists. Freight forwarders, 3PLs, and supply-chain operators use Expedock to digitize shipping documents, automate back-office workflows, and scale operations without scaling headcount. Customers include Maersk, Gebrueder Weiss, and large shippers such as Nike, Adidas, Coca-Cola, and Shell. Expedock is backed by Insight Partners. The company operates a Digital BPO offering and document-automation product suite; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: LEAP
providers.description: LEAP is cloud-based legal practice management software for law firms, covering matter and contact management, document automation and court forms, time recording, billing, and trust accounting, tightly integrated with Microsoft 365. LEAP operates a LEAP Developer Console and LEAP Marketplace (developer.leap.build / console.leap.build) through which approved third-party developers build REST-based integrations (an "API Reference" is versioned there, e.g. v1.0.4, v1.0.5), but the technical reference - endpoint paths, base URL, and authentication schema - sits behind developer registration and an app review process rather than a public, self-serve API reference. There is no publicly published OpenAPI document, public base URL, or anonymous API key signup. Existing Marketplace integrations (Xero, Zoom, InfoTrack, LawTap, and others) confirm the API surface is real and in production use, but its concrete shape is not publicly disclosed.

providers.name: Turquoise Health
providers.description: Turquoise Health is a healthcare price transparency company (backed by a16z) that runs a platform aggregating and normalizing hospital and payer machine-readable price transparency files, negotiated contract rates, and out-of-network pricing into searchable, benchmarked rate data and analytics. Its products span rate analysis and benchmarking, contract management, clear rates and data assets, healthcare transactions, out-of-network pricing, patient cost estimates / Good Faith Estimates, and price-transparency compliance tooling, serving providers, payers, life sciences, and employers.

providers.name: Umony
providers.description: Umony is a London-based communications compliance platform, founded in 2017 and backed by Seedcamp, that captures, records, and archives employee voice calls, SMS, WhatsApp, and Microsoft Teams conversations at the telecom-network level for banks and other regulated financial institutions. Its platform spans the Umony App (BYOD softphone), Umony Mobile (eSIM carrier-level capture), and Umony Archive with AI risk scoring, and the company holds BSI-certified ISO 27001:2022, ISO 42001:2023, and ISO 22301:2019 certifications. Umony publishes no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: Civica Digital
providers.description: Cívica Digital is a Mexican civic-technology company, founded in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, that helps governments, public institutions, and organizations design, build, and launch digital services for citizens. Its product portfolio includes Urbem, a platform for digitizing government procedures and citizen-facing services; Signum, a digital document and official-records management system with electronic signatures; and a suite of conversational AI agents that support citizens over WhatsApp, phone, and web. The company focuses on digital government transformation across Latin America. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface has been located; this profile captures the company's public web presence, legal pages, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Darwin
providers.description: Darwin AI is an AI governance platform built exclusively for state, local, and education (SLED) government agencies, providing a centralized, secure hub for the public sector to safely adopt, manage, and govern AI tools while ensuring compliance, accountability, and public records requirements are met. The platform serves IT departments, innovation and digital services teams, city and county management, and data governance professionals across municipal and state government. Its core product surface includes the Control Center, which delivers cross-departmental visibility into AI usage along with records management and FOIA compliance tracking; the Policy Wizard, which helps agencies establish and refine AI policies aligned to regulatory requirements using 30+ policy frameworks and 15+ city and county regulation packs; Risk Management, which detects unauthorized or unvetted AI applications; the AI Navigator, which monitors departmental adoption patterns and surfaces actionable insights; and the Marketplace, an organization-wide hub of approved AI applications. Darwin AI was named to Government Technology's 2026 GovTech 100. The company also publishes a free public Policy Wizard tool. Darwin is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network as a government-sector company profile. As of this enrichment pass Darwin publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI, so this profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Diligent
providers.description: Diligent Corporation is a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company best known for its board management portal (Diligent Boards / Boardbooks) and the broader Diligent One Platform, which unifies board management, enterprise risk, audit, compliance, entity management, and ESG. The board portal itself is a security-hardened product with no public developer API - it is integrated through SSO (SAML 2.0), SCIM provisioning, and packaged connectors (Okta, Microsoft 365/Teams, Zoom, DocuSign). Diligent does, however, publish a real developer portal at developer.diligent.com covering the GRC side of the platform - the HighBond (Diligent One) REST API for audit/risk/compliance data, a GraphQL Entities API for legal-entity and subsidiary management, an ESG API for activity/usage data, and a Workflow API for jobs, tasks, and campaigns. API access is customer/partner-gated (a HighBond API key or SSO-scoped token is required) and pricing is quote-based via Diligent sales.

providers.name: Norm Ai
providers.description: Norm Ai (legal name Nomos AI, Inc.) is a legal and compliance AI company that embeds law and regulation directly into autonomous AI agents. Its platform spans Norm Law (an AI-native law firm), Norm Technology (domain-expert-built compliance agents), and Supervisory AI (systems that verify agent compliance), automating legal and regulatory workflows for financial institutions and enterprises. Backed by a $120M Series C round, it serves clients managing over $30 trillion in combined assets. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is currently published; this profile captures the company's security, compliance, and identity surface.

providers.name: Baton Media
providers.description: Baton is a music collaboration and IP-management platform for unreleased music, built by Baton Media Inc. (New York, Techstars '23). It gives musicians, producers, managers, and talent scouts tools to securely upload, organize, version, and share unreleased tracks, beat packs, and sample libraries across iOS and web. A proprietary media player shows creators exactly who is listening to their material, while collaboration spaces (private, invite-only, or public), an in-app audio studio (looping, pitch shifting, EQ, effects, sample pairing), and a creator-to-fan marketplace support discovery, placement opportunities, and monetization. Baton is building collaboration protocols to track IP rights and automate crediting and compensation across the creator economy. As of this enrichment the company publishes a consumer product (iOS app + web) with no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Bench IQ
providers.description: Bench IQ is a legal technology company building an AI-powered judicial intelligence platform that analyzes how individual judges reason and rule. Rather than limiting analysis to the roughly 3% of matters that produce written opinions, Bench IQ studies the reasoning behind all of a judge's rulings so litigators can anticipate decisions, craft stronger arguments, and shape case strategy. Founded by the team behind ROSS Intelligence — CEO Jimoh Ovbiagele and CTO Maxim Isakov — together with former Kirkland & Ellis restructuring partner Jeffrey Gettleman, the company says four of the top five AmLaw 100 firms rely on its analysis. It is backed by Battery Ventures, Inovia Capital, and Haystack, along with leading law firms including Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati, Fenwick & West, and Cooley.

providers.name: Descartes Underwriting
providers.description: Descartes Underwriting is a Paris-headquartered insurtech, founded in 2019, specializing in parametric insurance for climate, natural-catastrophe, cyber, and emerging corporate risks. It operates two complementary entities — Descartes Underwriting, a global parametric managing general agent (MGA), and Descartes Insurance, an ACPR-licensed European full-stack carrier — using AI, satellite imagery, IoT sensor data, and scientific risk models to structure index-based covers that pay out automatically within days when a predefined trigger is met, without a traditional claims-adjustment process. Backed by Battery Ventures and other investors, the company serves 600+ large corporations and public entities through corporate brokers across 20+ offices worldwide. No public developer API or documentation is published; the company distributes coverage through brokers rather than a self-serve API surface.

providers.name: Emtethal
providers.description: Emtethal is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia based smart compliance and inspection management platform for the food service and hospitality sectors, backed by 500 Global. The platform automates inspection scheduling and distribution, provides custom checklists per facility type, captures photo documentation with automatic timestamps and GPS location, detects and categorizes violations automatically, and pushes real-time alerts for critical issues. It layers analytics and compliance reporting on top of an offline-capable mobile field-inspection app (iOS and Android) and AI-powered camera and sensor monitoring. Emtethal serves both individual food facilities and consulting firms managing multiple client sites, offering a 14-day free trial. There is no public API, developer portal, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile is an API Evangelist company lead maintained for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Eversettled
providers.description: EverSettled is a digital estate-settlement platform that guides families through the probate process after a death. Positioned between expensive probate attorneys and overwhelming do-it-yourself paperwork, it combines an adaptive, state-specific estate checklist, automated asset discovery across bank accounts, insurance policies and subscriptions, subscription cancellation and debt negotiation, secure document organization, a dedicated human estate-care specialist, and Sage, a 24/7 AI probate assistant. Available across all 50 U.S. states, EverSettled is not a law firm and does not provide legal services. Backed by a $5M seed round led by Emergence Capital with participation from Seedcamp.

providers.name: Alexi
providers.description: Alexi is a Toronto, Ontario, Canada based legal artificial intelligence company that operates a private AI platform purpose-built for law firms, unifying legal research, drafting, and analysis into a single, single-tenant environment. Founded in 2017 by Mark Doble and a team of lawyers and technologists, Alexi specializes in litigation workflows — generating research memos grounded in primary law, identifying controlling authority and jurisdiction-specific requirements, framing case strategy, and producing persuasive first drafts that reflect a firm's voice, citation style, and approved structures. The platform also supports transactional work, document review and comparison, knowledge management, and firm-specific playbook application. Alexi's architecture combines a retrieval-first approach grounded in cited authority with agentic reasoning, delivered through a private cloud deployment so that firms retain ownership and sovereignty over their data, models, and workflows. Coverage spans all 50 U.S. states, Washington D.C., federal law, and all Canadian provinces and territories (excluding Quebec). The platform integrates with 20+ tools including iManage, NetDocuments, SharePoint, Elite 3E, Aderant, Litify, Actionstep, Filevine, Microsoft Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook, Zoom, DocuSign, Adobe Sign, Azure, AWS, Datasite, Intralinks, and Firmex. Alexi is SOC 2 certified, employs AES-256 encryption, and reports 99% uptime with customer firms including Dentons, Robins Appleby, Gluckstein Lawyers, MacLean Law, and Mongillo Law. The company's revenue model is SaaS subscription (Alexi Core and Alexi Advanced tiers); there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and integrations are delivered as turnkey enterprise connectors rather than a publicly documented integration platform.

providers.name: BlackSwan Technologies
providers.description: BlackSwan Technologies is an enterprise AI software company founded in 2014 by Michael and Elinoar Ouliel, headquartered in London with engineering across Israel, Poland and India. Its flagship product, ELEMENT, is marketed as an Enterprise AI Operating System: a low/no-code platform-as-a-service combining a data fabric, knowledge graphs, machine learning and composite AI so banks and other regulated enterprises can assemble applications for KYC on demand, enhanced due diligence, financial crime, transaction intelligence, market intelligence and underwriting without first consolidating their data. Its software engineering unit, BST LABS, built and open-sourced CAIOS (Cloud AI Operating System) and a family of Python developer tools (DynaCLI, CLVM, PyJdict, PyComposite, AuthK). BlackSwan Technologies was acquired by HUB Cyber Security Ltd. (NASDAQ: HUBC) in a stock-for-stock transaction that closed on 27 January 2025, and its corporate domain blackswantechnologies.ai no longer resolves in DNS; the secured data fabric technology is now marketed under HUB Technologies. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract (OpenAPI, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, MCP, A2A) was found for BlackSwan Technologies during enrichment.

providers.name: Harbor Global
