providers.description: Harbor Global is a global professional-services firm delivering technology, operations, strategy, and intelligence consulting to law firms, corporate legal departments, and government legal teams. Its practice areas span legal-technology and operations (application management, process automation, AI enablement), strategic advisory, intelligence and research/library services, and vendor governance, delivered by a global team of specialists. Harbor has grown through acquisitions such as iTrain (UK legal-technology training and AI enablement) and CE Global Partners (HCM/HR and payroll transformation). It is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. Harbor Global is a services company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company identity and discovery.

providers.name: Newgen Software
providers.description: Newgen Software is a global provider of NewgenONE, a unified low-code digital transformation platform that orchestrates content services (enterprise content management), business process management (BPM/workflow), and customer communication management (CCM) for banks, insurers, government agencies, and healthcare organizations. Founded in 1992 and headquartered in New Delhi, India, the company is publicly listed (NSE/BSE) and serves enterprises worldwide with document management, intelligent document processing, case management, and process automation. Platform capabilities are exposed to customers and system integrators via REST APIs, but Newgen does not operate a public, self-service developer portal or publish OpenAPI/SDK artifacts on its marketing site.

providers.name: Qiz Security
providers.description: QIZ Security is a cybersecurity company delivering a cryptography management platform for quantum-safe security. The platform helps organizations discover, prioritize, remediate, and govern their cryptographic assets across on-premises and cloud environments, making hidden cryptography visible and preparing them for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) adoption. Founded by experts in cybersecurity, networking, and post-quantum cryptography, QIZ Security is API-first and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, with offices in Lewes, Delaware (US) and Ra'anana, Israel.

providers.name: Spotlock
providers.description: Spotlock is a commodity risk management platform that helps organizations monitor, manage, and mitigate exposure to raw-material price volatility. It lets businesses track material exposures across inventory, customer contracts, and supplier commitments, set company-wide risk policies, and execute optimized hedging strategies — enabling fixed-price long-term contracts, profit margin protection, hedge accounting treatment, framework/agreement pricing, and global price intelligence for sectors such as construction and infrastructure, metal service centers and distribution, manufacturing and fabrication, automotive, energy, and transportation.

providers.name: Teamworks
providers.description: Teamworks is a sports technology company that builds "The Operating System for Sports" — an integrated software platform used by elite collegiate, professional, and national-team organizations to digitize the athlete lifecycle and consolidate their technology stack. The platform spans four product areas: Personnel (roster management, recruiting, scouting, player evaluation), Performance (strength & conditioning, nutrition, and a sports EMR / athlete-management system), Coaching (sport-specific game preparation and strategy for football, baseball, and hockey), and Operations (Hub communication, compliance, academics, inventory, camps, and influencer management), plus Wallet for athlete payments and Teamworks Intelligence for predictive analytics. Teamworks is a General Catalyst portfolio company. As of this profile the company exposes customer-facing SaaS products and a public status page but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Ohalo
providers.description: Ohalo is a data governance company whose Data X-Ray platform discovers, classifies, redacts, and governs unstructured data across enterprise file systems, databases, and cloud stores at petabyte scale. Using generative AI for content categorization and extraction, it helps organizations inventory sensitive data, audit access entitlements, automate redaction, and prepare their data estates for AI adoption while meeting regulatory frameworks such as GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS. Ohalo is backed by 500 Global, Anthemis, and Craft Ventures.

providers.name: Theom
providers.description: Theom is a cloud Data & AI Operations Center that governs and secures enterprise data estates, providing automated data security, compliance, and safe generative-AI data activation across multi-cloud environments. Founded in December 2020 by former Cisco, Google, and Yahoo security practitioners (creators of Tetration Analytics), Theom detects active data breaches, maps real-time data lineage, analyzes identity-aware data usage and insider threats, and enforces data-usage policy agentlessly. Its product spans Theom Core (data security and lineage), Theom AI (GenAI leak prevention), and Theom Trust (real-time data contracts). Theom is backed by Wing Venture Capital, Ridge Ventures, Snowflake Ventures, Databricks Ventures, SentinelOne Ventures, and M12, and was named a Leader in the 2026 Forrester Wave for Sensitive Data Discovery and Classification. Theom is delivered as an enterprise platform; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API docs.

providers.name: Hoptroff
providers.description: Hoptroff is a London-based precision timing company that delivers Traceable Time as a Service (TTaaS), providing enterprise-grade, traceable UTC time with guaranteed SLA accuracy to any data center or cloud environment. Founded in 2015 by Richard Hoptroff, the company operates a global network of atomic timing hubs in London, New York, and Tokyo, delivering microsecond-level precision over IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) and NTP. Its Certified Time and Terrestrial Time Feed products let organizations timestamp and audit automated events without a satellite dependency, using resilient multi-source feeds (three satellite feeds plus a terrestrial feed from the RISE Institute of Sweden) that are hardened against GPS spoofing and network failure. Hoptroff is certified to ISO 27001 and ISO 9001, and its time synchronization is licensed as an API so a consistent, compliant timescale can be applied across an enterprise for use cases in financial services (MiFID II timestamping and high-frequency trading), content streaming, gaming, IoT, and distributed ledger technology.

providers.name: Total Attorneys (Internet Brands)
providers.description: Total Attorneys is a legal marketing and lead-generation brand owned by Internet Brands. Originally a legal practice-management and client-intake SaaS backed by Bain Capital Ventures, the service was folded into the Martindale-Avvo network, and as of April 1, 2019 its attorney lead-generation offering transitioned to the Martindale-Nolo Pay Per Lead program. The totalattorneys.com site today markets pay-per-lead attorney marketing across practice areas such as bankruptcy, criminal defense, DUI/DWI, divorce, and personal injury. No public developer program or API is currently published.

providers.name: Auditocity
providers.description: Auditocity is an HR compliance software platform that helps organizations of any size master regulatory requirements and best practices. It maintains a library of more than 14,000 questions spanning federal, state, and industry-specific HR compliance, automatically generating custom-built audits tailored to an organization's industry, size, and location. The platform produces actionable findings reports that identify compliance gaps, tracks requirements across all 50 states, and delivers real-time regulatory updates through an HR technology partner network. Auditocity is a Techstars portfolio company. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification has been published at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ClassAction
providers.description: ClassAction operates enjin (集団訴訟プラットフォーム enjin), a Japanese class-action / group-litigation platform that connects consumers who have suffered damages from the same party with registered attorneys to pursue collective lawsuits. Victims report their damages, registered lawyers volunteer to take on cases, and participants share legal costs and evidence so that even small-value claimants can afford to litigate. The service launched in May 2018 and is free for users. This is a consumer-facing legal-tech website with no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Formality
providers.description: Formality is a Paris-based AI platform for end-to-end asset and contract intelligence, aimed at businesses that need to centralize, understand, and track their legal, administrative, and asset-related documents. The product covers the full contract lifecycle: AI-assisted creation and collaborative negotiation, electronic signature, then post-signature data extraction, deadline and obligation alerts, and natural-language analysis of the resulting document estate. Its AI is trained on corporate legal documents, works across multiple languages, and runs inside a secure perimeter with full auditability and no use of customer data for model training. Formality integrates with tools including Google Drive, SharePoint, DocuWare, Docusign, Universign, Yousign, HubSpot, Salesforce, Outlook, Teams, Slack, and Gmail, and runs on compliant hosting with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certifications and GDPR compliance. It was founded in 2023 and is backed by Partech, Serena, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: FundMiner
providers.description: FundMiner is a fund management and donor stewardship platform for mission-driven organizations, giving universities, healthcare systems, and community foundations one place to manage the full fund lifecycle. It combines fund management with compliance monitoring, impact and donor reporting, and a branded donor portal that gives donors real-time visibility into how their gifts are used. The platform integrates with existing financial systems and offers role-based dashboards and access controls. FundMiner is a Techstars-backed company; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API reference at this time, so this profile captures its public identity and web presence.

providers.name: Internet Brands
providers.description: Internet Brands is a KKR-owned digital media and software company, founded in 1998 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, that operates a portfolio of vertical franchises across health, dental, legal, and auto/home/travel markets. Its brands include WebMD and Medscape (health), WebMD Ignite and PulsePoint (health engagement), Henry Schein One and Dentrix (dental SaaS), FindLaw and Avvo (legal), and CarsDirect and Fodor's (auto, home, and travel). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and Redpoint Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. The holding company does not publish a single unified public developer API; developer surfaces live with its individual operating brands.

providers.name: Payall
providers.description: Payall Payment Systems provides purpose-built banking infrastructure that automates cross-border payments for regulated financial institutions. The platform orchestrates the full international money-movement lifecycle across originating banks, correspondent and clearing institutions, central banks, and payment channels, automating sanctions screening, KYC/AML compliance, fraud and risk management, FX, and settlement. Payall markets a lightweight, backward- compatible technical integration and business-friendly APIs (plus bulk/Excel upload) so banks, credit unions, EMIs, and other regulated institutions can offer safe, profitable international transfers. Public developer documentation and an open API specification are not published; the API surface at api.payall.com is authentication-gated.

providers.name: Sirius
providers.description: beSirius is an Amsterdam-based AI platform for the critical minerals and metals value chain. It builds a continuously verified digital Twin of every supplier, mapping each company's data to the frameworks, questionnaires, and regulations its buyers, auditors, and regulators require - including CSDDD, CMRT/EMRT/AMRT conflict-minerals reporting, EcoVadis, CDP, S&P CSA, UN Global Compact, LME Passport, and the Consolidated Mining Standard Initiative (CMSI). The platform automates supplier due diligence, sustainability and ESG data collection and verification, certification readiness, customer KYC, and ratings improvement across mining, processing, and trading supply chains, reducing manual audit and disclosure effort. beSirius is backed by Techstars and other investors.

providers.name: Edme Insurance Brokers
providers.description: Edme Insurance Brokers Ltd (formerly Aditya Birla Insurance Brokers, ABIBL) is an India-based composite insurance broker offering corporate, retail, and reinsurance solutions across 30+ industries including aviation, marine, energy, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, technology, and the BFSI and FMCG sectors. The company provides tailored risk management, employee benefits, and claims advisory services, backed by digital customer portals for policy and claims management and employee benefits. Edme is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Edme publishes no public developer program or API surface at this time.

providers.name: Indio Technologies
providers.description: Indio Technologies is a cloud-based insurance application and submissions platform for commercial insurance agencies and brokers, acquired by and now part of Applied Systems. Indio replaces manual PDF forms and spreadsheets with a library of 10,000+ digitally enhanced "smart" insurance forms and ACORD applications, a submission workspace that packages digital applications, schedule workbooks, document-upload requests and e-signature requests, plus secure document sharing. Indio does not publish a self-service public developer API. Programmatic access is partner/carrier-gated and delivered through Applied Systems - the Applied Epic bi-directional integration and SDK, the IVANS data exchange API (used to move submission and proposal data between agencies, brokers and carriers), and the Applied DevCenter partner developer program. The API surfaces below are modeled from Indio's documented product concepts (submissions, forms/applications, clients, documents and e-signatures); they are logical groupings, not publicly documented endpoints (endpointsModeled).

providers.name: Backstartup
providers.description: Backstartup is a Colombian tech-enabled accounting and legal services firm for startups and small businesses (notably SAS entities). It automated company formation, bookkeeping, tax filing, payroll, and legal/DIAN compliance for founders in Latin America. Backstartup has since been integrated into Numbi (numbi.ai), a tech-enabled accounting firm that operates monthly bookkeeping, taxes, payroll, and DIAN compliance on top of the accounting systems companies already use (Siigo and Alegra), pairing expert accountants with automation and AI. Backstartup's legacy domain (backstartup.com) now redirects to numbi.ai and Backstartup operates as a sub-organization within Numbi's Colombia operation. This is a services-company profile: no public developer API or OpenAPI is published. It entered the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Finbots.AI
providers.description: Finbots.AI (finbots.ai) is a Singapore-headquartered fintech offering CreditX, a no-code, AI-powered credit risk platform that lets banks and lenders build, validate, and deploy application, behavioural, and collection scorecards in hours instead of months. Its proprietary, explainable machine-learning models power real-time lending decisions in under 0.03 seconds, and the platform adds a Decision Engine (business rules), propensity modelling, and managed data services. Backed by Accel, finbots.ai serves retail banking, SME lending, and credit-card clients across APAC and MEA markets, and was among the first fintechs to complete Singapore's AI Verify AI-governance testing framework. No public self-service developer API is published; API integration is enterprise and sales-gated.

providers.name: Regbase
providers.description: Regbase is an AI-native regulatory intelligence platform that helps legal teams, compliance professionals, researchers, and government vendors monitor new and proposed laws worldwide. The platform uses AI agents to identify regulatory changes across 195 countries and 50 US states, surfacing draft bills, consultations, compliance requirements, and opportunities like grants from hard-to-find government sources, non-English publications, and informal channels that traditional tools miss. Regbase then analyzes those changes automatically and alerts users to updates relevant to their practice areas, spanning employment and labor, AI governance, healthcare, privacy, climate and sustainability, government contracting, and other regulated industries. Founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Spring 2026 batch, Regbase is based in San Francisco. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist network; at the time of enrichment Regbase publishes a login-only web application and no public API, developer documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: TrademarkNow
providers.description: TrademarkNow is an AI-native trademark clearance, screening, and watching platform, now part of Corsearch. It helps brand owners and legal teams create, launch, and defend trademarks globally using neural-network models that analyze phonetics, spelling, meaning, and visuals to surface conflicts across trademark registries. Its modules include ExaMatch for preliminary screening across 190+ registries with phonetic matching, NameCheck for instant trademark risk assessment, LogoCheck for deep-learning image-based logo conflict clearance, and Portfolio Analyzer for portfolio-strength benchmarking and coverage-gap analysis. TrademarkNow is delivered as a SaaS web platform (login at tm.corsearch.com) and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Apiday
providers.description: Apiday is an ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) software platform built for private markets. It combines AI-powered automation with expert guidance so investors, fund managers, and portfolio companies can streamline sustainability reporting, comply with regulatory frameworks (SFDR, EU Taxonomy, EDCI, PRI, ILPA), automate ESG questionnaires and due-diligence requests, calculate GHG emissions against 3,000+ benchmarks, and turn ESG obligations into measurable value creation. The company reports that over 500 investors and 5,000 companies use the platform across private equity, venture capital, private credit, institutional LP, and infrastructure asset classes. Backed by Speedinvest. Apiday does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Payna
providers.description: Payna is a compliance operating system for financial licensing that automates applications, renewals, maintenance, and monitoring across all 50 US states and jurisdictions. It tracks state statutes, NMLS procedures, and FinCEN requirements in real time, calculates filing deadlines backward from due dates, scores compliance posture against state examiner playbooks, automates document pre-fill and e-signature, and maintains a timestamped, queryable audit trail for examinations. Payna serves regulated financial sectors including money transmission, lending, mortgage, cryptocurrency/VASP, debt collection, loan origination, and insurance. It is a Y Combinator (W26) company; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Mercanis
providers.description: Mercanis is an AI-powered procurement platform that automates the end-to-end source-to-contract lifecycle for enterprise procurement teams. It combines structured intake, connected sourcing (RFx and supplier comparison), supplier relationship management, contract lifecycle management, and risk, compliance and spend analytics, coordinated by a large fleet of autonomous AI agents. Mercanis serves sectors including energy and utilities, pharma and chemicals, automotive, consumer goods, manufacturing, and construction, and integrates with ERP systems such as SAP and NetSuite alongside procurement networks like Unite. The company is headquartered in Germany with SOC-certified, GDPR-compliant infrastructure. No public developer API, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface has been identified as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Scarlet
providers.description: Scarlet is Europe's only Notified Body specialised in software and AI-based medical devices. Operating at scarlet.cc, Scarlet certifies Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and AI as a Medical Device (AIaMD) under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), streamlining conformity assessment, CE marking, and certificate transfers for manufacturers who ship iteratively and release frequently. Backed by Creandum, Scarlet was built to bring modern, fast-moving regulatory certification to AI and software medical-technology companies. Scarlet is a regulatory and certification services provider; it currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Wenspiredata
providers.description: Wenspiredata is an enterprise cybersecurity vendor delivering all-in-one, zero-trust Privileged Remote Access Management (RPAM) for high-risk access. Its platform secures and governs remote privileged access for IT, OT, and third-party vendors, including air-gapped and industrial (OT) environments, and pairs with OsecT for OT-native intrusion detection and continuous visibility. Wenspiredata also offers security assessment services (external attack surface and internal vulnerability assessments) and helps organizations across manufacturing, telecom, finance, and healthcare meet regulatory compliance requirements. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment; the company markets a demo-led enterprise product and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Florence Healthcare
providers.description: Florence Healthcare provides eRegulatory and clinical-trial site enablement software for research sites, sponsors, and CROs. Its eBinders product is an electronic investigator site file (eISF) and participant binder platform that replaces paper regulatory binders with structured, compliant, 21 CFR Part 11 workflows; eTMF manages the sponsor-side trial master file; and SiteLink connects a network of 10,000+ investigator sites across 44+ countries to sponsors and CROs for remote site access, monitoring, document exchange, and source data verification. Florence describes an "open API" for eBinders, eTMF, and SiteLink that supports connected management of roles and permissions, inbound and outbound document exchange, and document status reporting across regulatory and source documents. Access to the API is partner- and customer-gated - it is granted through Florence's integration and partnership programs rather than a self-service public developer portal, and no public API reference, OpenAPI description, or base URL is published as of this writing.

providers.name: Kerys
providers.description: Kerys Software is a European (Palaiseau, France) cybersecurity company behind YS::Desktop, a Type 1 hypervisor that runs multiple fully isolated environments on a single workstation. By preallocating dedicated CPU cores to the hypervisor versus VM workloads and adding hypervisor-level encryption, YS::Desktop closes VM escape and cross-VM attack vectors while sustaining roughly 92% native performance. It replaces dedicated admin machines, air-gapped OT laptops, and traditional VDI for regulated organizations in aerospace and defense, energy, finance, construction, and the public sector, with a mandatory Security Domain model (no unmanaged VMs) administered through the YAC console. The company positions around NIS2, IEC 62443, and ANSSI multi-environment workstation guidance and sells 100% through resellers. Kerys does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or pricing; it was surfaced as a Seedcamp portfolio company and enriched here from its public site.

providers.name: Juleb
providers.description: Juleb is a Saudi Arabia-based pharma-tech and retail software company providing an integrated cloud platform for the health, retail, and distribution sectors. Its suite spans accounting and financial management, inventory and warehouse management, sales force automation (SFA), point of sale (POS), Rx e-prescription, e-commerce, and DSCSA regulatory compliance. Juleb connects to Saudi compliance systems (ZATCA/Fatoora, RSD, GS1, Wasfaty), e-commerce channels (Salla, Shopify, HungerStation), payment providers (Geidea, Alhamrani), and ERPs (Microsoft Dynamics). Founded by Yousuf Jamjoom and backed by 500 Global, Juleb exposes a REST API (documented at docs.juleb.com) covering inventory, point of sale, prescriptions, and partner/company resources.

providers.name: Loctax
providers.description: Loctax is a collaborative tax compliance, risk, and governance platform built for global in-house tax teams. Founded in 2020 and based in Gent, Belgium, its Global Tax Intelligence Platform lets teams ask any tax question grounded in their own company data and IBFD's authoritative tax content spanning 220+ jurisdictions, then act on the answer with workflow, compliance-monitoring, risk, and controversy-management tooling. Loctax is backed by Index Ventures, Cavalry Ventures, and Seedcamp, and in 2026 was acquired by Tax Systems to build a combined EMEA tax-technology platform. Loctax is a closed enterprise SaaS product with no public developer API, portal, or specification at the time of this profile.

providers.name: ELV8
providers.description: ELV8 Inc. operates Scout, a financial platform built for college athletes and athletic departments navigating Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) income. Scout provides NIL income tracking and management, financial education with one-on-one coaching, payment processing for schools (per diems, bonuses, and NIL payments), roster cap-management and compliance tooling, and business-setup assistance such as LLC formation and tax filing. ELV8 Inc. is an SEC-registered investment adviser and works with 30-plus college athletic programs serving thousands of athletes. It was surfaced as a Techstars-backed portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. Scout is a consumer/institutional fintech product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Quantifind
providers.description: Quantifind is a financial crimes automation company founded in 2009 by physicists Ari Tuchman and John Stockton to extract meaningful risk signals from large, unstructured datasets. Its flagship SaaS platform, Graphyte, applies machine learning, natural language processing, and entity resolution to anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) compliance. Graphyte spans watchlist and sanctions screening, adverse media screening, enhanced due diligence, credit risk, and investigations, and is delivered through GraphyteSearch (an investigation application), GraphyteQueue (an AI-native case manager), GraphyteAPI (a synchronous REST risk-assessment API), and GraphyteBatch (batch screening). Quantifind serves Tier 1 and regional banks, digital banks, Fortune 50 companies, and federal and defense agencies, and integrates with case-management systems such as Oracle FCCM. Backed by a16z.

providers.name: Recyda
providers.description: Recyda is a German software company offering an all-in-one platform for packaging sustainability and regulatory compliance. The platform centralizes packaging data, automates Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) fee calculation and declaration across 20+ countries, and assesses packaging recyclability against standards such as the ZSVR Minimum Standard and EN 18120. It supports EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) compliance, portfolio-wide assessments, and submission-ready reporting, turning weeks of manual compliance work into minutes. Recyda is trusted by global brands and is backed by venture firm Speedinvest.

providers.name: Remedio
providers.description: Remedio is an autonomous cybersecurity remediation platform that detects and automatically fixes misconfigurations, configuration drift, and emerging Shadow AI risks across hybrid IT environments at machine speed. Its platform spans five modules — Baseline (secure configuration baselines), AI Govern (discovery and governance of AI tools, agents, and connections), Fortify (autonomous vulnerability and misconfiguration remediation), Gate (application and software control), and Assure (continuous compliance monitoring) — with predictive impact preview, auditable rollback, and ROI measurement. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. Remedio publishes a marketing site and blog but no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Sware (fka BTR)
providers.description: Sware (formerly BTR) is a life sciences software company providing AI-driven GxP validation for regulated life sciences and pharmaceutical organizations. Its Res_Q SaaS platform combines a decade of validation intelligence with a Data Cloud and AI agents that automate validation work, surface insights, and keep every decision explainable, traceable, and reversible. A companion product, GxPNext, delivers agentic validation built for software development so teams can embed GxP validation directly into their applications, ship faster, and simplify customer audits. Sware serves quality, regulatory, and engineering leaders across software validation, AI/ML validation, plant and equipment validation, and medical device / SaMD development, and publishes SOC 2 and ISO 9001 certifications. It is backed by Insight Partners. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI is available today (the Res_Q API page is password-gated), so this profile captures the company's public identity, compliance posture, and domain-security probe.

providers.name: Divebell
providers.description: Divebell is a cloud-native data privacy and security compliance platform that helps organizations discover, classify, and protect sensitive data and personally identifiable information (PII) across their data sources. The platform pairs continuous, intelligent data scanning with "Deep Automation" to deliver four capability areas: Data Discovery (data classification, data mapping, and access management), Compliance Automation (risk assessment, data retention, and regulatory compliance), DSR Fulfillment (data subject request workflows, subject mapping, and automated retrieval), and Risk Protection (a policy engine, "Risk Sonar," and remediation actions). Delivered as a lightweight modern SaaS with private data processing, Divebell protects customer data across sources such as Snowflake and AWS. Divebell was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and is now part of the Exterro family, operating as Exterro Data Discovery.

providers.name: Eve
providers.description: Eve (eve.legal) is a legal AI platform built by Butler Labs, Inc. for plaintiff law firms. Marketed as "the only legal AI that works your whole case with you," Eve 2.0 is positioned as a proactive AI workforce that spans the full plaintiff case lifecycle — intake and evaluation, pre-litigation drafting (medical chronologies, demand letters), litigation discovery (propounding and responding), and case auditing. The platform is organized around three product surfaces: Eve Agents (intake & evaluation, AI voice agent, medical overviews, demand letters, drafting, propounding discovery, responding to discovery), Eve Auditor (nightly audit of the active caseload for missed value drivers such as TBIs, MRIs ordered but not taken, and mass-tort eligibility), and Eve Analyst (announced as "coming soon"). Eve targets personal injury and labor & employment plaintiff firms and claims to be used by 1000+ firms with reported outcomes including a 250% year-over-year revenue increase, 2.5x case capacity, 90% faster demand letter generation, and a 4.9/5 G2 rating. Eve is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and HIPAA compliant, with case data encrypted, isolated per-firm, and never used to train shared models. The company is led by founder & CEO Jay Madheswaran (formerly Rubrik, Lightspeed Venture Partners), co-founder & CPO Matt Noe, and co-founder & Head of Engineering David Zeng, and has raised $164M+ from venture investors. Eve is a closed B2B SaaS application; as of this profile there is no public developer API, no public OpenAPI/AsyncAPI documentation, no `docs.eve.legal` developer portal, no SDKs, and no public repositories under the `eve-legal` GitHub organization (the org exists with zero public repos as of May 2026). All access is through the Eve web application following a sales-led "Schedule a call" / "Book a Demo" motion.

providers.name: Forwardlane
providers.description: ForwardLane Technologies builds Signal Studio, a decision intelligence platform that transforms enterprise data into auditable actions rather than dashboards. Users ask questions in natural language and receive Next Best Actions with complete audit trails in seconds, powered by a semantic data layer, multi-agent AI orchestration, a no-code signal builder, and in-database processing so data never leaves the customer environment. Validated across eight years of Fortune 500 production, Signal Studio serves financial services, private credit and private equity, real estate, energy and oil and gas, and government, with BYOK support for any LLM, cloud, or inference provider. Led by CEO Nathan Stevenson. ForwardLane exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PharmaCCX
providers.description: PharmaCCX, operating as CCX (Contingent Commitment Exchange), is a digital market-access and pricing software company for the pharmaceutical industry, serving pharma manufacturers, payers, and health systems. Its enterprise platform provides a single source of truth for global pricing strategy and contract management through three products: CCX Planning (contract scenario planning, modeling, and analysis), Deal Admin (contract administration and pharma-payer coordination), and CCX Digital Negotiation (an invite-only deal negotiation tool). The platform is delivered as an invite-only enterprise SaaS terminal (marketaccess.ccxterminal.com) with Terminal and Sandbox environments; no public developer API, documentation, or portal is published as of this profiling.

providers.name: Spring Labs
providers.description: Spring Labs is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial institutions, deploying autonomous AI agents that complete operational work rather than only surfacing insights. Its agents score customer-service calls, run 100% QA/QC review coverage, identify and file complaints, and (soon) automate the dispute lifecycle, alongside SummerGRC, an AI-driven governance, risk, and compliance product. Spring Labs targets sponsor banks, fintech lenders, enterprise banks, BaaS platforms, and debt-collection (ARM) organizations. Originally a blockchain-based data and identity company backed by Multicoin Capital, the firm has repositioned around applied AI for regulated financial operations. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes a marketing/product site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Eisen
providers.description: Eisen is an AI-enabled compliance operations platform for financial institutions and digital asset companies, managing escheatment (unclaimed property), disbursement, customer outreach, and 1099 tax reporting across all account types. Its product suite includes an Escheatment Manager that tracks state compliance deadlines and dormancy rules, a Disbursement Manager that automates personalized customer payments, an Outreach Manager that re-engages dormant account holders, and a 1099 Reporting Manager for tax reporting. Eisen handles dormant accounts, stale checks, account wind-downs, and forced closures, and is backed by Cowboy Ventures, Homebrew, and Index Ventures. As of this profile Eisen exposes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this record captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Lexyom
providers.description: Lexyom (Lexyom LLP) is a law firm operating at lexyom.com, which redirects to lexyomlaw.com. The firm markets legal services to financial-services companies: financial institution setup, company registration, broker licensing, proprietary-trading ("prop firm") licensing, trademark registration and IP protection, retainer representation, and contract drafting and review. Published offices are New York (450 Park Avenue) and Dubai (DIFC Gate Village), with stated emphasis on US and MENA cross-border regulation. The public web property is a client-rendered single-page application with a marketing site, a blog, a news section, a "Become a Client" intake flow, and an authenticated client portal (matters, contracts, documents, invoices, trademarks). Lexyom publishes no public API, developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: TrustArc
providers.description: TrustArc is a Walnut Creek, California enterprise privacy management platform that helps organizations operationalize global data privacy programs. Its product portfolio spans three suites. Privacy Studio covers consumer-facing consent and rights with Cookie Consent Manager, Consent & Preference Manager, Individual Rights Manager (DSR automation), and the Unified Trust Center. The Governance Suite covers internal privacy program operations with PrivacyCentral, Data Mapping & Risk Manager, Assessment Manager (PIA/DPIA/TIA), and Nymity Research for regulatory intelligence. Assurance Services delivers third-party attestations including Data Privacy Framework verification, GDPR and CCPA/CPRA validation, APEC CBPR/PRP, and TRUSTe Responsible AI Certification. TrustArc exposes a developer surface through gated APIs documented in the customer help center — including the Gateway API, Individual Rights Manager Rapid/Client APIs, Cookie Consent Manager Reporting API, Consent & Preference Manager Rapid/Standard APIs, and Assessment Manager Internal API — plus a Mobile Consent SDK (iOS), 300+ prebuilt connectors to platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Adobe Experience Manager, Microsoft Dynamics, Jira, and Google Workspace, and a Google Consent Mode v2 template published on GitHub. Founded over 28 years ago and serving 1,500+ enterprises including Abbott, ADP, GE, Nike, and Starbucks, TrustArc operates on a commercial SaaS model; complete API specifications are not publicly available.

providers.name: Flank
providers.description: Flank builds AI agents for enterprise legal teams that handle high-volume, routine legal work autonomously. Its supervised agents operate like paralegals, taking in requests via email or portals, executing contracting tasks against an organization's own templates and playbooks, and returning completed work for lawyer review. The platform covers drafting, contract review, negotiation, and triage, letting legal departments insource repetitive work while lawyers supervise finished output and high-risk items. Flank is backed by HV Capital, Insight Partners, and Speedinvest, and is SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 42001, GDPR, and CCPA compliant.

providers.name: Axis 2
providers.description: Axis (axis.xyz) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2022) knowledge base platform for corporate affairs, government relations, and compliance teams that helps large companies understand their markets and regulatory obligations across the world. The platform delivers regulatory intelligence for international expansion - which laws to comply with and which officials to seek approvals from - spanning 40+ countries and 200+ industries across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. This is a product SaaS company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Finch Legal
providers.description: Finch Legal (Finch) is an AI-powered pre-litigation platform built for personal injury law firms, combining US-based expert legal operators with AI agents to run cases on autopilot from intake through demand. Its services span 24/7 bilingual intake and client sign-up, insurance claim and police-report retrieval, treatment tracking with client check-ins, and expert-reviewed demand-letter generation, with beta capabilities for medical chronologies and litigation support. Finch writes updates directly into a firm's existing case-management system rather than adding a new tool, integrating with Filevine, Smokeball, Litify, Neos, SmartAdvocate, MyCase, Clio, Casepeer, and Cloudlex. The company is SOC 2 certified, headquartered in New York City, and backed by venture investors. Finch exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK at this time; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Porters
providers.description: Porters is an AI-native outsourcing partner for European banking operations. Its platform uses AI agents with human oversight to automate high-volume back-office banking processes — account seizure processing (private and public account seizures), insolvency case management from intake to resolution, and chargeback dispute data collection, triage, and resolution. Documents are ingested, extracted, and classified; decisions are made with a human in the loop; and banking actions plus audit reports are generated automatically. Porters hosts data in the EU in line with GDPR, maintains 24/7 audit trails, and does not use customer data for model training. It was founded by veterans of McKinsey, Qonto, Upvest, Solaris, and Roland Berger, and is backed by Earlybird and Seedcamp. No public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Simple Legal
providers.description: SimpleLegal is an enterprise legal management (ELM) platform for corporate legal departments, providing legal spend management, e-billing, matter management, vendor management, accruals, and reporting and analytics. It helps in-house legal teams track outside counsel spend, review and approve invoices, manage matters, and report on legal operations. Founded as a venture-backed legal operations startup (backed by a16z) and now part of Onit's enterprise legal management product suite, SimpleLegal is delivered as a cloud application at app.simplelegal.com. The product exposes an authenticated REST API to customers for integration with financial and matter systems, but does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI description, or API reference; its only standalone public discovery surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt and a vulnerability disclosure program operated through Onit.

providers.name: Akorda
providers.description: Akorda was a contract intelligence and contract lifecycle management (CLM) startup that applied artificial intelligence and natural language processing to accelerate contract negotiation, review, and management for legal and procurement teams. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company built machine-learning tooling to surface risky clauses, benchmark contract language against standards, and streamline the redlining and approval workflow. Akorda has since been acquired and absorbed into LegalSifter: its former domain (akorda.com) now redirects to legalsifter.com, and no independent Akorda product, developer portal, or public API remains. This profile is retained as a network lead and reflects the acquisition rather than a live, standalone API provider.

providers.name: Alethea
providers.description: Alethea is an AI-powered risk intelligence company that operates a proactive narrative and disinformation risk management platform. Its flagship product, Artemis, is a threat intelligence and narrative-risk mitigation platform that detects coordinated inauthentic behavior, influence operations, and emerging online narratives before they escalate into reputational or operational crises. Complementary offerings include Risk Radar (a threat-visibility dashboard), an agentic AI takedown agent for automated mitigation, and Alethea Insights macro threat analysis. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and Multicoin Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. Alethea is an enterprise, engagement-led platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a self-service developer portal.

providers.name: Anaqua
providers.description: Anaqua provides intellectual property management (IPMS) software and services for corporations and law firms, unifying patent, trademark, and broader IP portfolio operations through process automation, business intelligence, and analytics. Its AQX platform (AQX Corporate, AQX Law Firm, AQX Pharma) is complemented by PATTSY WAVE portfolio analytics, AcclaimIP patent search, ideaPoint innovation management, and IP services such as annuity, renewal, foreign filing, and docketing. Clients include Adidas, ARM, TSMC, and GSK. Backed by Insight Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners, Anaqua does not currently publish a public developer API or portal; integration is handled via its SeeUnity application-integration technology.

providers.name: Atticus
providers.description: Atticus is a consumer legal-technology law firm, launched in 2019 and backed by Forerunner Ventures, True Ventures, and GV, that helps Americans in crisis get the benefits and aid they deserve. It began with Social Security Disability and has expanded to workers' compensation, VA benefits, and other government-aid programs. Atticus combines a free online qualification quiz, on-staff lawyers and client advocates reachable by phone, text, or chat, and a matching engine that connects each client with vetted attorneys from a network of 100+ top firms who work on contingency. It has helped tens of thousands of people access billions of dollars in life-changing aid. Atticus is a consumer-facing service company and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Concentric AI
providers.description: Concentric AI provides an AI-driven data security governance platform built on its proprietary Semantic Intelligence technology to autonomously discover, classify, monitor, and protect sensitive data across cloud and on-premises environments. The agentless platform spans Data Security Posture Management (DSPM), data loss prevention, data access governance, insider risk detection, and generative-AI data security (covering Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, and Perplexity), connecting to 40+ data platforms and business applications including Snowflake, Amazon S3, Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Google Workspace. Backed by Homebrew, Concentric AI was recognized as a 2026 Gartner Peer Insights Customers' Choice for DSPM.

providers.name: conrizon
providers.description: conrizon AG is a German holding company, founded in 2020 and headquartered in Essen, that unites four of Europe's leading Enterprise Content Management (ECM) brands - easy software, PROXESS, HABEL, and Portal Systems (Shareflex), alongside the friendWorks professional-services unit - under one roof. The group provides legally compliant, audit-proof digital archiving (GDPR, GoBD, eIDAS), document management (DMS), invoice and procure-to-pay (P2P) processing, contract management, and HR/HCM software with automated workflows, plus AI services and connectors for SAP and Microsoft 365 / SharePoint. Solutions are offered cloud-native, in a private cloud, on-premises, or hybrid, and are relied on by more than 8,700 companies and organizations worldwide. conrizon is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It publishes a corporate marketing site but no public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Klaimee
providers.description: Klaimee is a Y Combinator (Spring/P26 batch) startup building certification, financial guarantee, and liability insurance for AI agents running in production. The company evaluates an autonomous agent across risk dimensions such as scope, data exfiltration, unauthorized action, output integrity, adversarial manipulation, behavioral stability, model drift, and operational control, then issues a letter-graded certification report with remediation guidance and a Klaimee-Verified badge that AI vendors use to clear enterprise procurement. Certified agents are backed by a financial guarantee and by AI liability insurance priced against the certification score, covering the gap that traditional errors-and-omissions and cyber policies explicitly exclude — hallucinated outputs, unauthorized actions, data exposure, prompt injection, and wrongful commitments. Klaimee also runs a public adversarial-testing playground where teams can stress-test an agent with probes for prompt injection, jailbreak, decision drift, data leakage, and biased outputs. Klaimee currently sells a human-delivered certification and underwriting service; it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer documentation as of this enrichment pass. Founded in 2026 by Ines Boutemadja (CEO) and Julien Catonnet (CTO), based in San Francisco.

providers.name: OnCorps AI
providers.description: OnCorps AI is an agentic AI platform for fund operations at financial institutions, automating complex middle- and back-office tasks through AI agents that predict root causes and reduce time and cost. Its products span NAV oversight, investment operations, reconciliation, financial report review, performance verification, security attribution, cash and positions validation, accounting controls, OTC confirmations, and FX/share-class hedging, plus Deep Industry Research Agents (DIRA) for financial transaction analysis. OnCorps serves asset managers and fund administrators including PIMCO and Natixis, and is SOC 1 and ISO 27001 certified. No public API or developer program is currently published; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PathSpot
providers.description: PathSpot Technologies provides a health-and-safety operating system for restaurants, commercial kitchens, food manufacturers, cafeterias, and hospitality venues. Its flagship HandScanner uses light-based spectroscopy to detect harmful contaminants on employees' hands in about two seconds after washing and drying. Alongside the scanner, PathSpot's SafetySuite bundles real-time temperature monitoring (PowerTemp), digital task management (PowerTasks), and food labeling (PowerLabels), rolling the data up into the SafetySuite Hub dashboard with analytics, automated compliance reporting, email reports, text alerts, and optional API-based data integration. PathSpot markets API integration as a data-delivery feature of SafetySuite but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDKs as of this profile.

providers.name: QuSecure
providers.description: QuSecure is a post-quantum cybersecurity company whose QuProtect R3 platform helps enterprises and government agencies discover, remediate, and report on cryptographic risk ahead of the quantum-computing threat. The platform pairs Recon (automated inventory of cryptographic assets), Resilience (crypto-agile remediation of encryption without code changes or downtime), and Reporting (Cryptographic Bill of Materials / CBOM for NIST, FIPS, CNSA 2.0, and GDPR compliance). QuSecure serves telecom, defense, finance, and critical-infrastructure customers including Fortune 500 companies and U.S. federal agencies. This profile currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Scorpion
providers.description: Scorpion is an American marketing technology company that provides revenue-focused advertising, marketing, and software services to local and multi-location businesses in home services, legal, franchise, and healthcare verticals. Founded in 2001 by Rustin Kretz and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Utah (with major operations in Valencia, California), Scorpion pairs done-for-you digital advertising and SEO with its own AI-driven platform. In 2024 it launched RevenueMAX, an AI marketing platform built on Scorpion AI that aligns marketing spend, intake, and long-term revenue, and in 2025 it introduced Scorpion Convert, an AI intake-and-conversion product that automates response, scheduling, and voice/messaging engagement for missed leads. Scorpion is a services-and-platform provider; it does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: nPlan
providers.description: nPlan applies machine learning to construction project schedules to forecast and de-risk large capital projects. Trained on a large corpus of historical project schedules, its products (nPlan Insights Pro and nPlan Portfolio) analyze programme risk, benchmark schedules against similar projects, and surface the interventions most likely to keep delivery on time and on budget, with a Power BI integration for portfolio-level project controls. nPlan is a private enterprise SaaS company backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Vector Legal
providers.description: Vector Legal is an AI-native law firm and legal operating system for startups, combining senior startup attorneys (averaging 10+ years of Big Law experience) with proprietary software for formation, fundraising, commercial contracts, employment and equity, and M&A, priced around outcomes rather than billable hours. Legal services are provided by Vector Legal, P.C., a licensed California law firm; the platform is built by Vector Systems, PBC. A Y Combinator Winter 2026 company headquartered in San Francisco, also backed by Base10, Palm Drive Capital, and Amino Capital.

providers.name: Autositu
providers.description: Autositu (AutoSitu) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) PropTech startup building an AI-native intelligence layer for real estate development plan review. Its multi-agent platform automatically analyzes site plans, building plans, and AEC drawings against municipal zoning and building codes to flag compliance issues before submission, cutting city comments and resubmittals so approvals move faster. The product serves cities, architecture and engineering firms, and real estate developers with human-in-the-loop review workflows. Autositu is an early-stage SaaS company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Collabra
providers.description: Collabra (Collabra Pty Ltd, ABN 35 672 933 818) is an Australian enterprise AI automation company whose platform combines robotic process automation with large language models to run back-office operations — contract review, revenue assurance, financial operations, vendor management, data processing, and compliance monitoring. Its product suite is CollabraCore (isolated, segmented data-protection workspaces), CollabraGuard (an AI-safety layer that constrains LLM output to prevent hallucinations and errors while logging every action), and CollabraFlow (a rapid build-test-deploy environment for automation workflows). The public tagline is "AI you can trust to run your operations". As of this profile Collabra is a demo-led SaaS with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Demander Justice
providers.description: Demander Justice (demanderjustice.com) is a French legal-technology company that lets everyday people (justiciables) resolve disputes and take a matter to court without hiring a lawyer. Through simplified, guided online procedures it helps users send formal notices (mise en demeure), file injonctions de payer, and bring cases before the relevant French courts across consumer, housing, telecom, travel, banking, neighbor, and small-claims disputes. The service combines legal information fiches with a step-by-step document-generation and court-filing workflow. Backed by Partech; profiled in the API Evangelist network under the Consumer sector. No public developer/API surface was found at enrichment time.

providers.name: i2x
providers.description: i2x is a German real-time AI platform for contact centers, built by i2x GmbH in Mönchengladbach. It provides live agent assistance that surfaces contextual recommendations during calls in under 0.4 seconds, including automatic detection of purchase signals and faster agent onboarding; full-coverage call analysis with automatic transcription plus quality, compliance, and sales-opportunity scoring across 100% of conversations; and voicebots for automated inbound/outbound telephony and virtual agent-training scenarios. The platform emphasizes DSGVO/GDPR compliance with EU-only hosting in German data centers, prepared works-council documentation, and EU AI Act alignment, positioning itself as an alternative to US-cloud-dependent conversation-intelligence tools. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are currently published; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of hv-capital.

providers.name: Model N
providers.description: Model N is a revenue management software company that has served the pharmaceutical and medtech industries for more than 25 years. Its cloud commercial platform helps life sciences innovators grow market access, optimize revenue, and maintain regulatory compliance across provider and payer management, US Government Pricing and Medicaid, global pricing and tender management, 340B vigilance, state price transparency, deal management, and its Intelligence Cloud and Data nSights analytics. Model N is enterprise SaaS with a customer support portal and knowledge center but no public developer API surface; this profile captures the company identity plus its published security, trust, and compliance posture.

providers.name: Pollen
providers.description: Pollen Technologies is a London-based, FCA-authorised white-label fintech platform that lets any business launch its own banking and payments product with no code and a fully managed back office. The platform delivers programmatic payment delivery, instant named IBAN account opening, third-party bank account linking for real-time balances and transaction data, multi-currency payments across 148 currencies into more than 160 countries, local payment schemes, and virtual and physical cards. A managed compliance layer covers KYC, AML, transaction monitoring, client fund safeguarding and help-desk support under SLAs. Pollen Technologies Ltd is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 (firm reference 768011), founded in 2015 and backed by Seedcamp, Level39 and Q-Advisers. Access to the underlying payments and banking APIs is delivered as a managed, partner-only service rather than a public self-serve developer program, so no public API specifications, SDKs or developer portal are currently published.

providers.name: Closure
providers.description: Closure (Closure Intelligence, Inc.) builds an AI-powered digital analyst platform for law enforcement agencies that securely transcribes, translates, searches, organizes, and analyzes case evidence — jail communications, warrant returns, and large multi-lingual case files — to help investigators overcome evidence overload and resolve homicides and cold cases. The platform runs under a zero-access security model with SOC 2 Type II, CJIS, and HIPAA compliance. Backed by CRV. No public API or developer program is currently published.

providers.name: Witness AI
providers.description: WitnessAI is an AI security and governance platform that lets enterprises safely deploy and manage AI across their workforce. Its platform spans three pillars: Observe (visibility into all AI activity, shadow-AI discovery, and cataloging of applications and agents), Control (governance policies, audit trails, and compliance across human and AI workforces), and Protect (runtime security that blocks prompt injection and jailbreaks and filters harmful outputs). It addresses data leakage, prompt-injection attacks, unauthorized agent activity, and compliance gaps. The company is backed by GV. As of this profile no public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published; engagement is via sales/demo.

providers.name: Netreveal
providers.description: Netreveal is BAE Systems Applied Intelligence's financial crime detection and prevention platform, providing analytics for anti-money laundering, fraud detection, sanctions screening, and regulatory compliance for banks and financial institutions. Netreveal does not currently publish public developer-facing APIs; integrations are typically delivered through customer engagements.

providers.name: Noetica
providers.description: Noetica AI is a New York-based legal and financial market-intelligence platform that uses natural language processing and a proprietary knowledge graph to extract, benchmark, and analyze deal terms from millions of public and private transactions. It serves transactional attorneys, capital-markets and M&A lawyers, credit and private-lending professionals, and legal-innovation teams at leading global law firms, delivering real-time quantitative and qualitative benchmarking across 60+ transaction types. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Thomson Reuters Ventures. As of this profiling Noetica exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface; it operates as an enterprise B2B SaaS platform.

providers.name: Aizome
providers.description: Aizome is an enterprise AI agent security and governance platform that makes autonomous AI agents accountable through identity-led access control and intent validation. Its platform follows a three-step model: Discover (map every AI agent in the enterprise, including undocumented ones), Assess Risk (score agents by data access, functionality, and behavior), and Control and Govern (enforce policy through identity-led governance and intent interception before execution). Aizome inherits agent identity from users scoped to specific tasks and integrates with existing enterprise identity systems such as Okta, Microsoft Entra, and SailPoint rather than replacing them. It targets enterprise workflow automation use cases including billing, talent reviews, contract monitoring, and customer service. Aizome is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. No public API, developer portal, or OpenAPI specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Arcos Labs
providers.description: Arcos Labs is an early-stage, stealth-mode legal technology company focused on "rethinking the practice of law." Backed by 8VC as a portfolio company, the firm is building software aimed at modernizing legal work, and is currently operating in pre-launch / early-access mode with a public waitlist rather than a generally available product. As of this profile there is no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDK surface — only a marketing site, a careers page, and an early-access intake form. This record was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with the identity details the company publishes today; API artifacts will be captured if and when Arcos Labs ships a developer offering.

providers.name: Gambit
providers.description: Gambit Security is an Israeli cyber-resilience company, founded in 2024 by Unit 8200 veterans Alon Gromakov (CEO), Sa'ar Elias (CPO) and May Kogan (CTO), that emerged from stealth in February 2026 with $61M in seed and Series A funding from Cyberstarts, Kleiner Perkins and Spark Capital. Its product, Balens, is an AI-native autonomous resilience platform that continuously maps every resource in an environment into end-to-end business applications, revealing dependencies, backup coverage and immutability, detecting infrastructure drift, scoring Cyber Resilience Posture Management (CRPM) and validating real-world recovery paths against ransomware and outages. It also automates compliance evidence for frameworks such as DORA, NIST CSF and SOX. Gambit does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal.

providers.name: Springcoin
providers.description: Springcoin (operating as Spring Labs) is an AI-native compliance and customer-experience platform for financial services. It builds autonomous AI agents for contact centers, quality assurance, complaint handling, and dispute resolution, alongside SummerGRC, a governance, risk, and compliance product with entity intelligence and an agent builder. The platform integrates with 50+ contact-center and CRM systems and was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or open documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Trayd
providers.description: Trayd is a construction payroll, HR, and compliance platform built for commercial trade contractors and subcontractors. It automates certified and prevailing-wage payroll, union and multi-state compliance reporting, field and labor tracking, crew scheduling and dispatch, HR onboarding and benefits, and offers same-day pay, moving tens of millions of payroll dollars each week. Founded in 2022 (Y Combinator S23) and backed by Bloomberg Beta, Trayd operates a private SaaS and mobile application with no public developer API, documentation, or integration surface published at this time.

providers.name: Basel III
providers.description: Basel III is a comprehensive global regulatory framework developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) in response to the 2007-2008 financial crisis. It strengthens bank capital requirements by requiring higher quality and quantity of capital (CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital), introduces new liquidity standards (LCR and NSFR), adds a leverage ratio backstop, and includes countercyclical capital buffers and G-SIB surcharges. Basel III implementation in the EU/UK is delivered via CRD IV/V and CRR regulations. The final Basel III package (sometimes called Basel IV) addresses output floor and credit risk model constraints introduced in 2017.

providers.name: OnPlan
providers.description: OnPlan (onplan.co) publishes guidance and content on project controls, budgeting, and forecasting for organizations managing projects and capital programs. The site covers cost planning and budget management, risk management frameworks, change control procedures, earned value management, and benefit realization tracking across infrastructure, construction, and technology projects. It is presented as an informational and educational resource rather than a self-service SaaS platform: at the time of enrichment the public surface consists of a homepage, a blog of dated articles, a contact page, a privacy policy, and a sitemap, with no developer portal, public API, documentation, pricing, sign-up/login, or terms-of-service pages exposed. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched from the live site; no machine-readable API artifacts were found to harvest.

providers.name: Lattice Health
providers.description: Lattice Health is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) healthcare company building AI governance as a managed service for hospitals. The platform sits beside an existing clinical stack and taps the HL7 and DICOM signals that deployed imaging and clinical AI models already emit, with no rip-and-replace integration, then continuously measures population drift (PSI), subgroup fairness disparity under HHS Section 1557, latency against target, and silent vendor model-update detection across every vendor model running in production. Rather than another dashboard, Lattice delivers a per-role signed PDF report each morning to IT directors, CMIO/CIO, and compliance officers, cryptographically signed with the institution's own signing key so any recipient, including outside counsel or a regulator, can verify the artifact offline with standard open-source tooling and no Lattice account or infrastructure. Radiologist thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback on AI results is aggregated at model level and folded into the next morning's findings. The company positions itself around standards alignment (IHE UPS-RS work-list status, AI-Results and ERA classification, ONC HTI-1, FDA Predetermined Change Control Plan envelopes with automatic breach detection) and HIPAA-safe egress with a strict-mode PHI redactor, deployed on-premise or in the customer's private cloud so PHI stays behind the hospital firewall. As of this profile Lattice Health publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification, SDKs, or pricing; it is a pre-public-API company tracked here as an AI governance and clinical AI oversight lead.

providers.name: Poetic
providers.description: Poetic is an enterprise AI automation company whose platform learns an organization's rules and procedures and then executes end-to-end business processes with high precision and compliance. Marketed as "turn your business into software," Poetic ingests procedures, training materials, and expert feedback to build self-healing automations that adapt when underlying systems change, targeting long, multi-step workflows such as fraud detection, KYC, and dispute resolution. The company emphasizes enterprise-grade security with zero data retention (processing data in-transit only) and states SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, HIPAA, and GDPR compliance, and cites customers including AIG, SoFi, and Chime. Poetic is an early-stage, Kleiner Perkins-backed AI company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: TrustAI
providers.description: TrustAI (trytrust.ai) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator Summer 2026 company founded in 2026 by Hannah Chung and Medha Venkatapathy that provides continuous compliance, governance, and risk assessment for AI agents operating on sensitive enterprise systems, with an initial focus on ERP agents such as SAP Joule. It maps what every agent can reach, then runs evaluations across six domains - data privacy, hallucinations and grounding, permission compliance, robustness at scale, accountability, and security - including adversarial pentests and prompt-injection red-teaming, and maps every risk to controls like SOX, ITGC, ISO 27001, GxP, and the EU AI Act for audit-ready reporting. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, docs, or SDKs. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub.

providers.name: Alinia Ai
providers.description: Alinia is an AI compliance and control platform that helps enterprises deploy large language models and AI agents safely and in compliance with regulations, making AI systems "compliant by design" through regulation-informed control layers. The platform is built around three products: an Evaluation Engine that tests AI systems against company policies and regulatory standards (compliance red teaming), Guardrails that enforce compliance in real time — including a proprietary multilingual RAG Guard model that blocks hallucinations and irrelevance — and Monitoring that provides automated auditing, full traceability, and compliance reporting of AI activity. Alinia is model-agnostic and multilingual, targeting financial services, healthcare, and other heavily regulated industries, with named customers including Banco Santander and Origin Financial. The company was co-founded by Ariadna (CEO, previously Head of ML Platform at Twitter and Director of Development at IBM Watson) and Carlos (COO, previously AI Counsel at Hugging Face), operates offices in Barcelona, Valencia, New York, and Pittsburgh, and is backed by Speedinvest. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP
providers.description: Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP is a global Am Law 10 firm with approximately 2,200 lawyers and 39 offices across North America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. The firm provides corporate, transactional, litigation, and regulatory services across energy, financial services, healthcare, life sciences, retail and ecommerce, sports, technology, and transportation, with widely recognized depth in employee benefits and executive compensation, fintech and financial services regulation, intellectual property, and M&A. Morgan Lewis does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or machine-readable data product; its public technology surface is limited to its corporate website, an email-alert subscription managed through a Real Magnet (REACTION) marketing platform, and a portfolio of LexBlog-style practice blogs covering specific subject areas.

providers.name: Innovatrix Tech, Corp.
providers.description: Innovatrix Tech, Corp. operates Sahl (getsahl.io), an AI-powered Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform built in the MENA region for MENA organizations. Sahl automates policy generation, control mapping, risk assessment, evidence tracking, vulnerability scanning, and audit preparation across 20+ regulatory frameworks including PDPL, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, NCA ECC, and SAMA CSF, aiming to reduce compliance work from months to weeks with an AI DPO assistant and compliance copilot. The company was part of the Sanabil Investments x 500 Global Accelerator (Batch 8). It surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; as of this pass it publishes a marketing site and a customer application login but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Legora
providers.description: Legora is a Stockholm- and London-based legal AI company (formerly Leya) building a collaborative AI workspace for lawyers. The platform is centered on Legora aOS, an agentic operating system that connects information, communication, and the execution of legal work across Agent, Monitors, Lists, Legal Research, Tabular Review, Workflows, and the client-facing Portal, with Word and Outlook add-ins, an Editor, and a mobile app. Legora is sold to elite law firms and in-house legal teams via enterprise contracts; customers include Mannheimer Swartling, Goodwin Procter, Cleary Gottlieb, Linklaters, Bird & Bird, and HWL Ebsworth, with 400+ firms across 40+ countries. There is no public, self-serve developer API, SDK, or open-source release; integrations are arranged through enterprise sales and partnership engagements, and the platform runs on Azure OpenAI Service with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, GDPR, and HIPAA controls.

providers.name: Govport
providers.description: GovPort is a Software-as-a-Service platform built specifically for government contractors (GovCons) to manage subcontractor performance, compliance, and collaboration. It centralizes critical contract records, sends primes and subs automated requirements to keep every party compliant, and lets GovCons securely share and manage deliverables with one another across teams. Positioned as subcontractor management software for the federal contracting ecosystem, GovPort emphasizes high levels of data privacy and security. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and added to the API Evangelist network; the company references APIs in its terms of service but does not publish a public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Istante
providers.description: Istante is an Italian technology company (VAT IT03635230547, based in the Perugia area) that develops and operates Athena, a business-process-automation platform built around a team of specialized AI assistants. Athena covers assistants for communication routing and email classification, credit management and collections, a 24/7 voice/phone assistant, quote and order processing, automated tender monitoring and scoring, outbound lead engagement, contract and legal analysis, and HR and onboarding. It is positioned to collaborate with staff rather than replace them, keeping critical decisions under human oversight, and is offered on a fixed-cost "Digital Working Units" (DWU) pricing model rather than variable token pricing. The platform integrates across email, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, SMS, and phone, and is presented as GDPR and EU AI Act compliant. Istante was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: TakeCareOS
providers.description: TakeCareOS is an AI-powered operating system for home care and disability-services agencies. It consolidates fragmented back-office operations — shift rostering and scheduling, GPS-enabled clock-in/out, participant/client CRM, shift notes and incident reporting, timesheet management with variance detection, invoice generation synced to accounting tools (Xero, MYOB, QuickBooks), team messaging, and compliance and credential tracking — into a single platform. An AI assistant called Atlas drafts documentation, converts PDF forms to digital, and automates administrative work while requiring human approval. Founded by Ragav Sachdeva and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), the company is based in San Francisco and serves NDIS and Medicaid HCBS providers.
