As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Osmaura
providers.description: Osmaura is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-powered business development platform for corporate law firm partners. Its agents monitor the web, news, social media, and a firm's internal context to surface targeted new-matter opportunities, then recommend tailored outreach strategies. The platform works in three stages: building partner profiles from practice areas and networks, identifying prospective clients and their legal needs from external data sources, and suggesting engagement approaches for each opportunity. Founded by MIT graduates Kali Abeje and Jity Woldemichael. As of this profile the company publishes only a marketing landing page and a booking link — no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs exist yet. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting an API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Andco
providers.description: Andco is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-agent platform that automates the pre-litigation case workup process for personal injury law firms. Its agents retrieve and synthesize case documents across fax, phone, email, mail, web portal, and SMS channels, including police and accident reports, insurance coverage verification, medical records, and medical bills, then draft demand letters and calculate damages. Andco covers auto accident, premises liability, medical malpractice, workplace injury, and mass tort practice areas, offering same-day go-live and a free trial on the first case. This profile was surfaced from Andco's Y Combinator portfolio listing and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Andco publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification at this time.

providers.name: Denki
providers.description: Denki is a full-stack AI financial audit firm that automates internal audit work — planning, control testing, evidence collection, walkthrough interviews, and documentation — so teams can comply with financial regulations such as SOX 404 and BSA/AML. Its Tracer agent links general ledger, sub-ledgers, ERP, and payments data into a single audit trail, detecting anomalies early and producing ready-to-share audit packs. Denki works alongside existing systems such as AuditBoard, Workiva, and ERPs, and is built for audit teams at pre-IPO and publicly listed companies. Founded in 2025 by brothers Felipe and David Jin Li, Denki is a Y Combinator (F25) company that raised $4.1M led by Base10 Partners and Shine Capital.

providers.name: FilmTrack
providers.description: FilmTrack is a cloud-based content and rights management platform for the media and entertainment industry, streamlining the intellectual property lifecycle from project inception through distribution. Its software gives distributors and studios a holistic view of the data behind rights, availabilities, contracts, invoicing, licensing, revenue recognition, royalties, and workflow management. Founded in 1996 by Jason Kassin and headquartered in Studio City, California, FilmTrack was acquired by City National Bank in 2019 and now operates alongside Rightsline. Its API-first architecture enables integration with ERP and financial systems such as SAP and NetSuite, and an event bus for change-driven automation. Customers include Lionsgate, Miramax, Focus Features, Starz, and Screen Australia.

providers.name: Legora
providers.description: Legora is a Stockholm, Sweden-based collaborative AI workspace for lawyers, founded in 2023 as Leya by Max Junestrand (CEO), Sigge Labor (CTO), and August Erséus, and rebranded to Legora in 2025. The platform delivers an agentic operating system, Legora aOS, that helps law firms and in-house legal teams execute document review, legal research, drafting, advisory work, and regulatory monitoring at scale. Core product surfaces include Agent (end-to-end execution of complex legal work), Monitors (regulatory change tracking), Lists (workflow organization), Tabular Review, Workflows, Legal Research, Portal, Editor, a Word Add-in, an Outlook Add-in, and a mobile app, with practice-area solutions spanning M&A, litigation, banking, tax, and insurance. Legora is built on Azure OpenAI Service, holds ISO 42001, ISO 27001, and SOC 2 Type II certifications, operates under GDPR with EU and US data residency options, supports BYOK encryption, and commits not to train AI models on customer data. The company closed a $550M Series D led by Accel in March 2026 at a $5.55B valuation. Legora's commercial model is enterprise SaaS sold to law firms and in-house teams; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GitHub organization, or open-source release for the Legora platform.

providers.name: Mediacao Online
providers.description: MOL (Mediacao Online) is Brazil's first online dispute resolution (ODR) platform, founded in 2014 in Sao Paulo. It is a 100% digital, automated platform for negotiation, conciliation, and mediation that lets individuals, companies, and institutions resolve conflicts extrajudicially without going to court. The CNJ-compliant platform covers the full flow, from capturing cases in the courts, building agreement policies, sanitizing and enriching data, through to agreement approval and payment. MOL has facilitated tens of thousands of agreements and counts Magazine Luiza, Itau, and Caixa Economica among its clients. It is backed by 500 Global, Wayra, Canary, and Redpoint eventures. MOL exposes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Podqi
providers.description: Podqi is an AI-native intellectual property and brand protection platform that automatically detects and removes brand infringements across digital platforms. It scans major marketplaces, storefronts, and domains for counterfeit listings, stolen imagery, fake products, and copycat sites, then packages evidence and files takedowns at scale with minimal human intervention. The company reports roughly 95% AI automation with same-day detection and an average resolution time of about 1.2 days, and also operates Brandsweep.ai, a free public brand-protection scanning tool. Podqi serves brand owners, entertainment and creative companies, e-commerce sellers, and law firms. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Podqi publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Dealogic
providers.description: Dealogic is a global provider of content and software for the capital markets, including deal-management, analytics, league-table, and compliance solutions used by investment banks, sales/trading desks, and investment managers. Dealogic delivers data and connectivity primarily through its Cortex platform, Dealogic Connect, and Analytics products rather than a self-service public developer API; integrations are contracted with customers and accessed under license rather than from a public developer portal.

providers.name: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD.
providers.description: SCENARIO-X GLOBAL HOLDING PTE. LTD. (Scenario X) is a financial-technology company building an AI- and quantum-computing-powered platform for financial risk analysis, stress testing, and regulatory reporting. The integrated platform is organized into four modules — Scenario (adverse market-condition design), PPNR (Pre-Provision Net Revenue projection), Risk (market, counterparty, credit, and operational risk), and Console (financial-data aggregation) — plus a quantum-computing offering for predictive financial modeling. It serves banks, insurers, family offices, independent wealth managers, and commodity traders. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been found to date.

providers.name: InAuth (American Express)
providers.description: InAuth is a mobile-first digital device intelligence and authentication company acquired by American Express in 2018 and now operated within American Express's fraud-management portfolio; its technology also powers Accertify Device Intelligence. The InAuth Security Platform provides persistent device identification (device fingerprinting), malware and criminal-tool detection, rooted/jailbroken-device detection, location and behavioral risk analysis, and transaction risk scoring, delivered primarily through native iOS and Android SDKs embedded in merchant and financial-institution apps. Access is enterprise-gated through the Amex for Developers portal; there is no public self-serve REST API, OpenAPI specification, public package-registry distribution, or InAuth-specific public code repository for the product line.

providers.name: ISAAC Instruments
providers.description: ISAAC Instruments is a Canadian provider of in-cab technology and fleet management for the trucking industry - electronic logging devices (ELD), telematics, hours-of-service (HOS) compliance, driver workflow, messaging, and fuel/performance analytics, delivered as a fully managed hardware-plus-software platform. ISAAC runs an "Open Platform" with a documented API that lets fleets and 80+ integration partners (TMS/dispatch, maintenance, fuel tax, visibility, safety/compliance) share ISAAC data with their chosen vendors. API access is partner-gated - vendors apply through the ISAAC partner program and the full API Guide and reference live behind the ISAAC InRealTime portal and Client Center rather than on a public developer site. The API surface documented here is modeled from ISAAC's public platform and partner materials; exact endpoints, base URLs, and authentication are provisioned to approved partners.

providers.name: OpenEyes Insurance
providers.description: OpenEyes Insurance (OpenEyes Insurance Agency, Inc.) is an Austin, Texas-based insurtech startup, with an additional New York office, that provides commercial auto insurance for truck and bus fleet operators bundled with proprietary risk-prevention technology. Its offering pairs fleet coverage with real-time driver monitoring, AI dashcams, safety analytics, customized driver training, and 24/7 claims management, serving both insurance agents (For Agents) and fleet operators directly (For Fleets). Founded by Yoav Oron (CEO), Dr. Omry Sendik (CTO), and Dan Charash (Chairman), OpenEyes emerged from stealth in February 2023 with a $23M Series A led by Insight Partners with Pitango First. The company operates a customer-facing fleet dashboard but does not publish a public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Seamflow
providers.description: Seamflow builds AI-native software for the Testing, Inspection, and Certification (TIC) industry, automating end-to-end regulatory certification workflows for notified bodies and certification organizations while preserving human oversight and accreditation compliance. Its platform spans four core products: the Notified Body Suite (intake-to-certificate workflow management), Scheduling Agents (automated auditor assignment and travel optimization), Tech File Review (structured technical-documentation assessment against regulatory requirements), and Report Writing (AI-assisted drafting of compliance reports). Seamflow is an early-stage enterprise-SaaS company ($4.5M seed) backed by Initialized Capital and Northzone. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification; this record captures its verified public company surface.

providers.name: Patent Watch
providers.description: Patent Watch (PatentWatch.ai) is a Toronto-based, Y Combinator-backed (F25) legal-tech startup building AI for patent intelligence and infringement detection. Its platform interprets patents, maps them to competing products, and generates claim charts that show who is infringing and how, so IP teams can find licensing and litigation targets, send cease-and-desist letters, pursue counter-litigation, sell IP in wind-downs, and accelerate M&A diligence. It also runs AI invalidity and prior-art searches to help patents hold up in court. Founded in 2024 by Alexander and Andreas Stroe, the company raised a $2.8M seed round in April 2026. As of this profile Patent Watch is an early-stage product with a marketing site and login only, and no public developer, API, or documentation surface; this repo tracks it as an enrichment lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Procuri
providers.description: Procuri (procuri.ai) presents itself as an AI-powered procurement automation platform that uses specialized AI agents to discover and vet suppliers, optimize contract negotiation and pricing, monitor policy and regulatory compliance, and assess supplier and market risk for enterprise procurement teams. It was surfaced as a portfolio-lead stub of insight-partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass the public site publishes no developer/API surface (no docs, developer, API-reference, or OpenAPI pages resolve).

providers.name: Stealth Worker
providers.description: Stealth Worker is a cybersecurity staffing marketplace (Y Combinator W2016) that connects companies with vetted, contract-based information security, cloud security, privacy, and compliance professionals at competitive hourly rates. Engagements range from a few hours a week to full-time, covering InfoSec staffing, GDPR / data protection officer services, penetration testing, security architecture, SOC 2 / SOX / HIPAA / PCI audit and compliance, and CISO-as-a-service. Roughly 80% of consultants are US-based, with coverage across Europe, Asia, and Australia in 15+ countries. It is a professional-services company with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Fox Rothschild LLP
providers.description: Fox Rothschild LLP is a national US law firm with approximately 1,000 attorneys across 30+ offices. The firm has no public developer APIs. Its programmatic surface is limited to publication and content distribution: subscription-based email alerts and 21+ topical attorney-authored blogs hosted on the LexBlog (WordPress) platform, each of which exposes a standard WordPress RSS 2.0 feed at /feed/. This index catalogs the firm and the RSS-able LexBlog network as the consumable surface.

providers.name: SlideRule
providers.description: SlideRule is a no-code risk decisioning platform that lets risk and operations teams build, test, and deploy automated decision logic for fraud, credit, compliance, and trust-and-safety use cases without writing code. Its rules engine combines SQL and API data connectors, real-time analytics, A/B testing, backtesting, shadow mode, and case-management automation, and exposes a single API to trigger decision workflows. SlideRule has announced it is joining Block, Inc.; its standalone developer documentation surface (docs.sliderule.io) is no longer publicly reachable, so no live API specification could be harvested during enrichment.

providers.name: Medigram
providers.description: Medigram, Inc. is a healthcare AI governance company founded by Sherri Douville that builds Darwin, a governed decision platform for high-stakes clinical and performance AI. Darwin implements the sociotechnical data-governance architecture defined in IEEE UL 2933 (the six-dimension TIPPSS framework: Trust, Identity, Privacy, Protection, Safety, Security) and ANSI/HSI 2800:2025, scoring AI systems against a five-level maturity model and crosswalking them to ten governance frameworks (IEEE UL 2933, ANSI/HSI 2800:2025, ISO 42001, OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, NIST AI RMF, FDA, EU AI Act, and the HSCC guides). Applications include medtech AI governance, health-system IT review, and professional-sports player-health governance. Historically Medigram provided a secure, cloud-based mobile communication platform for healthcare professionals. Medigram is a portfolio company surfaced from the a16z network; it publishes marketing and standards content but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Alyne
providers.description: Alyne is a cloud-native governance, risk and compliance (GRC) platform, founded in Munich in 2015 and acquired by Mitratech in 2021, where it is now offered as Mitratech's Alyne. The platform pairs a large curated library of controls and regulatory content with AI-assisted risk assessments, control mapping, maturity scoring and reporting, helping enterprises and FinTechs manage cyber, operational and third-party risk. Alyne is delivered as SaaS through app.alyne.com and is positioned to integrate with common IT, compliance and data systems. As of this profile Alyne exposes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this record captures its public identity and probed domain security.

providers.name: ArcSight
providers.description: ArcSight is an enterprise security information and event management (SIEM) platform, now part of OpenText Cybersecurity (formerly Micro Focus, and HP before that). The ArcSight family centers on Enterprise Security Manager (ESM) for real-time correlation and threat detection, alongside Logger for log management and compliance, SmartConnectors for data collection and normalization, Intelligence for behavioral analytics, and Recon for search and investigation. ArcSight was an early Kleiner Perkins portfolio company. It exposes REST and web-services APIs (ESM client services, Logger Web Services, and SCIM user provisioning) primarily to on-premises and SaaS customer deployments rather than as a public developer platform.

providers.name: Formally
providers.description: Formally is an AI-native platform for legal collaboration that begins with US immigration. It combines intelligent technology, behavioral science, and secure, portable client data to connect immigration attorneys and law firms, individual visa applicants, and employers sponsoring global hires in a single connected product. Attorneys manage cases at scale, individuals track applications and reduce anxiety while retaining ownership of their own data, and employers coordinate visa sponsorship. As of this enrichment pass Formally does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, developer portal, or documentation surface, so this profile captures company identity and published web properties only.

providers.name: Lexoo
providers.description: Lexoo is a commercial legal services provider that operates as an outsourced in-house legal team for businesses, concentrating on commercial contract review and negotiation. The company handles routine contract work at fixed rates per agreement with a stated maximum two-day turnaround, so internal legal and sales teams are freed for more strategic work. Alongside contract review, Lexoo runs multi-country projects that engage local counsel across more than 70 countries for work such as terms and conditions localisation and regulatory research, and it builds playbooks and training materials that let client teams handle standard agreements independently. The practice is led by Nathalie Lambert and serves scale-ups and start-ups, with published client references including Trustpilot, Nielsen, ComplyAdvantage, Xeneta, Chattermill and Jokr. Lexoo is not an API-first company: it publishes no developer portal, documentation or SDKs, and its only machine-readable surfaces are the standard WordPress REST API and RSS feed exposed by its marketing site.

providers.name: PCI Compliance
providers.description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) is a set of security standards designed to ensure that all companies that accept, process, store or transmit credit card information maintain a secure environment. It plays a critical role in protecting organizational assets and maintaining a strong security posture. The PCI Security Standards Council does not currently publish a public REST API.

providers.name: Tongdun
providers.description: Tongdun (同盾科技 / Tongdun Technology) is a Hangzhou-based intelligent risk-control and anti-fraud analytics company whose public product presence now operates under the 小盾未来 (Xiaodun Future) brand at xiaodun.com. It uses AI and intelligent-analysis techniques to predict and score fraud and credit risk across consumer lending, banking, insurance, and e-commerce, delivering decisioning, anti-fraud, and risk-management capabilities to financial institutions, small-loan and consumer-finance lenders, auto finance, and internet businesses. Its risk-control services are consumed as enterprise interfaces (风控接口) provisioned behind account registration and sales onboarding; there is no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK registry surface exposed at this time. This record was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and enriched from the company's live public web presence.

providers.name: Atlas
providers.description: Atlas is an AI implementation partner built for independent accounting firms, deploying supervised, firm-specific AI "junior accountants" that automate repetitive, data-intensive workflows such as client onboarding, follow-ups, bookkeeping, compliance, and financial reporting while keeping human accountants in control of every decision and client relationship. Founded by Arpit Maheshwari (CEO) and Jagmal Singh (CTO) and co-led by Accel and Stellaris with Felicis participation, Atlas raised a $6M seed round in 2026 to scale its network of partner firms across North America. Atlas is currently a services-led AI company and publishes no public API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: DOT Regulations
providers.description: Department of Transportation regulations governing the safe transportation of hazardous materials and other commercial transport activities in the United States. These regulations help organizations meet regulatory requirements and demonstrate accountability to stakeholders.

providers.name: K2 Integrity
providers.description: K2 Integrity is a global risk, compliance, and investigations advisory firm specializing in financial crimes risk management, regulatory compliance, fraud detection, asset tracing and recovery, cybersecurity and AI resilience, crypto and digital-asset solutions, internal audit, and independent monitoring. It serves financial institutions, corporations, governments, and law firms worldwide. K2 Integrity was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; this profile has been enriched but the firm publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Kovr.ai
providers.description: Kovr.ai is a security and compliance automation company surfaced through the Battery Ventures portfolio and profiled in the API Evangelist network. Its verified public engineering presence is the GitHub organization github.com/kovr-ai, whose open-source kovr-aws-nist-compliance project validates AWS environments against NIST 800-53 Rev 5 and NIST 800-171 Rev 2 and maps findings across the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark, MITRE ATT&CK, OWASP Cloud Security, the AWS Well-Architected Framework, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the CSA Cloud Controls Matrix, the SANS Critical Security Controls, and NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture, running roughly 160 checks across 50+ AWS services. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification has been located for this company; the corporate website is served behind a bot-protection interstitial that blocks automated retrieval, so link properties beyond the homepage and the GitHub organization remain unverified.

providers.name: Smartsign
providers.description: Smartsign (SmartSign) is a Brooklyn, New York-based e-commerce retailer of customizable signs, labels, and tags for regulatory, compliance, and safety applications, founded in 1999. It sells pre-designed and custom signage - safety, parking, traffic, property, and facility signs, plus banners and labels - online to businesses of all sizes, including a large share of the Fortune 1000 across education, healthcare, and industrial verticals. Norwest Venture Partners acquired the company in 2019 and Sentinel Capital Partners acquired it in September 2022. SmartSign operates as a business-to-business and business-to-consumer e-commerce storefront and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Traderion
providers.description: Traderion is a fintech company that combines technology and gamification to build digital learning platforms for banks and financial institutions. Its products include a gamified sales and trading simulator covering equities, FX, bonds, and commodities with AI-powered feedback, a MiFID II regulatory-compliance training platform built as a virtual simulated bank, and a risk-profiling platform for identifying and detecting risky behavioral patterns within organizations. A Seedcamp portfolio company, Traderion does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Alphora Holdings
providers.description: Alphora (Alphora GmbH / Alphora Holdings) is a Berlin-based, AI-native managed IT services company founded in 2025 and backed by Northzone at the seed stage. Its agentic platform runs IT operations end-to-end for businesses and managed service providers (MSPs) — an integrated IT service desk, managed compliance and documentation, managed AI delivered by forward-deployed engineers, endpoint cybersecurity, user and hardware provisioning, and 24/7 network and cloud monitoring — pairing centralized intelligence with local execution across a shared data lake. The company operates alphora-it.com with a marketing site and active careers portal but does not yet expose a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Bayshore
providers.description: Bayshore (bayshore AI GmbH) is a Munich-based legal and compliance technology company building an agentic AI platform that turns any ruleset — from sector regulations to internal corporate policies — into deterministic, machine-readable guardrails for AI agents. Positioned as a "Legal & Compliance Front Door," the platform handles incoming requests from business teams, auto-clears low-risk cases with instant responses, escalates complex matters to human reviewers, and maintains audit-ready documentation for every decision. Founded in 2024 by Paul F. Welter, Philipp Wiegand, and Erik Krauter, the company focuses on highly regulated industries including finance (MaRisk, DORA, NIS2), pharma, defense (export controls, sanctions), and cross-industry programs (GDPR, anti-bribery, antitrust, third-party due diligence). Bayshore raised an $8M seed round led by Earlybird Venture Capital in 2026. This profile currently exposes no public API, developer portal, or specifications.

providers.name: Eigen
providers.description: Eigen Technologies is a London-based intelligent document processing (IDP) and data-extraction company that uses natural language processing, object detection and machine learning to extract, classify and interpret structured data from unstructured documents at scale. Its no-code platform lets teams in financial services, insurance, law and professional services pull hundreds of datapoints out of contracts, loan agreements and filings to manage risk, automate processes and meet regulatory obligations, with extracted data pushed downstream via its document-processing API. Founded in 2014 and backed by Goldman Sachs, Temasek, Lakestar, Dawn Capital, ING Ventures, Anthemis and the Sony Innovation Fund, Eigen was acquired by contract-lifecycle-management platform Sirion in June 2024.

providers.name: ElMetr
providers.description: ElMetr (المتر) is a Middle East legal-tech company providing online legal consultation and guidance for companies, entrepreneurs, and individuals. The platform combines licensed lawyers with modern technology to connect users with qualified legal help, offering subscription legal packages that cover company formation and registration, contract review, compliance, intellectual property, and dispute resolution. Founded in Egypt and now operating in Saudi Arabia, ElMetr aims to make legal work clear, fast, and fair so businesses can move faster and reduce risk from first idea through expansion. ElMetr is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This company profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; ElMetr does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Seafair
providers.description: Seafair is an AI-native ERP platform for maritime operations, unifying crew management, HSQE and regulatory compliance, technical maintenance (planned maintenance systems and defect tracking), and accounting into a single system for shipping companies and ship managers. Its AI compliance engine performs document search and framework reviews (such as DryBMS and TMSA) and embeds AI assistance directly into operational workflows. Seafair markets itself as API-first with fast ERP integrations, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition. Seafair is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Equator Principles
providers.description: The Equator Principles is a risk management framework adopted by financial institutions for determining, assessing, and managing environmental and social risk in project finance transactions. It provides a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring to support responsible risk decision-making and is primarily intended to provide a minimum standard for due diligence and monitoring in project finance and related advisory activities.

providers.name: EvenUp
providers.description: EvenUp is a SaaS company building proactive AI for personal-injury law firms, spanning the full case lifecycle from intake and treatment management through demand drafting, negotiation, discovery, and trial support. The platform combines AI drafting, communication agents, medical record management, proactive workflows, and executive analytics on top of integrations with popular case-management systems. EvenUp reports serving more than 2,000 personal-injury firms and processing roughly 10,000 cases per week, with more than $10B in damages claimed through the platform. The company is venture-funded (Series E) at a $2B+ valuation, with backing from Bessemer, B Capital, Bain Capital, Lightspeed, Premji Invest, and others. EvenUp does not publish a public developer portal; integrations are delivered through case-management partner connectors rather than a self-serve API.

providers.name: Image API
providers.description: Image API was a digital business automation company specializing in the digitization, optimization, and management of business processes, forms, and content. The company has rebranded as Docufree and provides enterprise services including document scanning and imaging, digital mailroom automation, business process automation (RPA/AI), electronic signature, cloud document management, and outbound print and mail. Despite the legacy brand name "Image API", the company does not publish a public developer API or API portal. This repository tracks APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Lawdingo
providers.description: Lawdingo is a New York City legal-technology company founded in 2012 by Nikhil Nirmel and Dan Langevin, and a Y Combinator Winter 2013 alum backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst and AltaIR Capital. It launched as a consumer marketplace for talking to a lawyer on demand, then pivoted to serving law firms and corporate legal departments with remote paralegals and contract attorneys — legal research, litigation drafting, court filing and discovery support — delivered through an online platform where clients assign work, share documents, deposit funds and track hours. Lawdingo publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs, and as of this enrichment pass its lawdingo.com and www.lawdingo.com domains both return HTTP 404 "Site Not Found" from an unpublished Framer site, leaving no live web surface to harvest.

providers.name: Shepherd 3
providers.description: Shepherd is a Y Combinator-backed (W21) insurtech modernizing commercial insurance for the construction and renewable energy sectors. Using technology and data-driven underwriting, it delivers faster decisions and clearer risk insights across Primary Casualty, Excess Casualty, and Builder's Risk coverage for middle-market to enterprise builders and operators. As of this enrichment pass Shepherd does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, MCP server, or a developer portal — this profile captures the company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Potion Labs
providers.description: Potion Labs (which rebranded its engineering org to Ntropika Labs) is a decentralized finance team behind Potion Finance / Potion Protocol, an on-chain risk-management and options platform on Ethereum. Potion is a "perfectly priced put AMM" — a decentralized put-option / DeFi insurance marketplace where liquidity providers earn yield by selling downside protection through a proprietary bonding curve based on the Kelly Criterion, while buyers get automated routing to the best price across independent liquidity providers. The protocol is delivered as Solidity smart contracts with TypeScript/Vue frontends rather than a hosted REST API. Backed by Polychain Capital. This profile was surfaced from Polychain's portfolio and enriched from the team's public GitHub org and website; the project appears largely dormant (contracts deployed to the deprecated Ropsten testnet, and potion.fi now serves a DeFi blog).

providers.name: Vouch
providers.description: Vouch is a San Francisco-based business insurance brokerage built for startups and high-growth companies, headquartered at 250 Montgomery Street, Suite 650. Co-founded by Sam Hodges and Travis Hedge, Vouch positions itself as the insurance broker for leaders building what's next, with the tagline "Ambition Insured." The company has raised $225M+ from Ribbit Capital, Redpoint, Y Combinator, Index Ventures, and other investors, and serves more than 6,000 insured companies across four industry verticals: Technology (AI, SaaS, Fintech, Cybersecurity, Hardware, DevTools, eCommerce, Crypto), Healthcare & Life Sciences (HealthTech), Financial Services (Venture Capital, Hedge Funds, Asset Management), and Professional Services (Architecture/Engineering, Management Consulting, Accounting, IT Consulting, Creative). Vouch's offering combines a tech-enabled brokerage workflow — including same-day quoting for 81% of submissions — with programs covering founder and investor protection, contract requirements review, workforce compliance, comprehensive coverage review, and claims advocacy. Vouch operates as an insurance broker rather than a developer platform and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer portal; its only public GitHub artifact is Quadipy, a small Python utility for transforming structured data into RDF graph format, indicating an internal knowledge-graph practice but no externally consumable API surface.

providers.name: Cozen O'Connor
providers.description: Cozen O'Connor is a full-service U.S. law firm founded in 1970 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with more than 1,000 attorneys across 33+ offices in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The firm is ranked among the top 100 law firms in America and is best known for its nationally recognized subrogation, insurance, labor and employment, global corporate, intellectual property, and government relations practices. Cozen O'Connor Public Strategies, the firm's bipartisan federal, state, and local government affairs and lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. and major state capitals. The firm operates an unusually broad thought-leadership network of LexBlog/WordPress-powered blogs and podcasts (subrogation, cyber law, health law, state AGs, transformative AI, OSHA, employment law, family law, property insurance, casualty coverage, real estate / land use, professional responsibility, and a Public Strategies feed), each of which exposes a standard `/feed/` RSS endpoint. Cozen O'Connor does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization. This profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface — practice and industry pages, attorney directory, ancillary businesses, lobbying arm, and the blog/podcast RSS network — rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Lexmark International
providers.description: Lexmark International is a global imaging and IoT solutions leader that helps customers worldwide realize the full potential of their information through printers, multifunction devices, and managed print services. As of 2024, Lexmark was acquired by Xerox Holdings Corporation. Public developer APIs are not currently advertised through an open developer portal.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Governata
providers.description: Governata is a Saudi Arabia-based data governance and management platform that helps government entities and enterprises turn complex data into business value through comprehensive, PDPL-aligned data management. Its product suite spans Data Governance (business glossary, data catalog, data classification, data lineage, metadata store, data quality), Master Data Management (domains, golden record, matching and survivorship), Data Privacy (personal-data discovery and protection under Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law, access management, and a service catalog), and Governata Core, an administrative backbone covering license management, audit trail, and workflows. Governata packages role-based solutions for chief data officers, compliance officers, data protection officers, and data stewards, and sector solutions for government, healthcare, financial services, insurance, telecom, retail, energy, and large enterprises. It is backed by 500 Global and is being profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found at the time of enrichment; this profile captures the company's identity and web presence.

providers.name: INTL FCStone
providers.description: INTL FCStone Inc. (rebranded as StoneX Group in 2020) is a Fortune 100 financial services organization providing execution, risk management, advisory services, market intelligence, and post-trade services across asset classes and global markets including commodities, equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, and securities.

providers.name: LICENSE.md
providers.description: File specifying the legal license under which a project is distributed, defining permissions, conditions, and limitations for use and redistribution. Standard reference for SPDX-identified open source licenses including MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0, BSD, and Creative Commons variants.

providers.name: Paisley Consulting
providers.description: Paisley Consulting was a governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) software company best known for its AutoAudit internal audit management product. The Paisley Consulting brand and its paisleyconsulting.com domain now redirect to Empowered Systems, a GRC software vendor whose Connected Risk platform delivers internal audit, internal controls, enterprise risk, operational risk, third-party risk, model risk, and policy & compliance management, along with the AutoAudit audit solution. The company supports frameworks including SOX/ICFR, COSO, Basel III, NIST, ISO 27001, and DORA. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public API, SDK, or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: FM (FM Global)
providers.description: FM (formerly FM Global) is a mutual insurance company specializing in commercial and industrial property insurance, loss prevention engineering, and risk management research. FM operates through six business units including FM, FM Affiliated, FM Approvals, FM Boiler Re, FM Cargo, and FM Renewable Energy, and is one of the largest commercial property insurers in the world. This repository tracks the FM (fm.com) entity and any APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable artifacts. The abbreviation "FM" is also used in unrelated contexts (Facilities Management, FM radio broadcasting, financial management); this repository is scoped to the FM Global commercial property insurer that owns the fm.com domain. No public APIs or developer programs are currently published.

providers.name: Marsh & McLennan
providers.description: Marsh & McLennan Companies is a global professional services firm offering clients advice and solutions in risk, strategy, and people through Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer, and Oliver Wyman. The firm does not currently publish a public developer portal or self-service APIs; data exchange with clients is conducted through engagement-specific integrations.

providers.name: Ndata
providers.description: nData (ndata.cz) is a European pharmaceutical software company operating since 2005 that builds GxP-compliant, AI-assisted systems for the pharma lifecycle: portfolio and project management (ePM), regulatory affairs (eRA), quality control planning (eQCP), artwork and packaging management (eAW), controlled documentation (eDOCS), clinical trial documentation / eTMF, plus eLAB (R&D lab operations), and eGO and eTRANSFER (launching Q3/2026). Its public web presence is a marketing and product-catalog site; nData publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specifications. Note: this repo was seeded as a bain-capital-ventures ai-infrastructure portfolio stub, but the ndata.cz surface is a pharmaceutical GxP software vendor — the portfolio match appears to be a mismatch.

providers.name: Blank Rome LLP
providers.description: Blank Rome LLP is an Am Law 100 U.S. law firm founded in 1946 and headquartered in Philadelphia, with approximately 600+ attorneys across roughly 14 U.S. offices plus an international presence (Shanghai). The firm provides comprehensive legal and government-advocacy services across commercial and corporate litigation, corporate / M&A and finance, restructuring and bankruptcy, government contracts, intellectual property, labor and employment, real estate, tax, white-collar defense, matrimonial and family law, and a nationally recognized maritime and international trade practice. Blank Rome Government Relations LLC, the firm's affiliated lobbying arm, operates from Washington, D.C. The firm publishes practice-area client alerts, the Mainbrace maritime newsletter, and industry insights through its website's News & Events and Publications sections. Blank Rome does not operate a public developer program, REST/GraphQL API, SDK ecosystem, or GitHub organization; this profile catalogs the firm's public-facing knowledge surface (practice pages, newsletters, alerts) rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Clausematch
providers.description: Clausematch is a London-founded regulatory technology (RegTech) company providing a cloud platform for policy and procedure management, regulatory change management, and structured document authoring and collaboration for banks, insurers, and other regulated financial institutions. Its tooling helps compliance teams draft, review, version, and attest to policies while mapping regulatory obligations to internal controls. Clausematch was acquired by Corlytics in 2024; the clausematch.com domain now 301-redirects to corlytics.com. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. No public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment (the web surface is WAF-protected and returns HTTP 403 to automated probes).

providers.name: Kira Systems
providers.description: Kira Systems is a machine-learning contract analysis and review platform for law firms and corporate legal teams, automatically extracting clauses, concepts, and data points from contracts during M&A due diligence, real estate, banking, and other transactional work. Founded in Toronto and backed by Insight Partners, Kira was acquired by Litera in 2021 and is now offered as Litera Kira. It integrates with HighQ and Intralinks data rooms and Litera Transact, and exposes an Open API for additional customer integration needs; no public developer portal or OpenAPI specification is currently published.

providers.name: Otrafy
providers.description: Otrafy is an AI-powered supplier management platform that automates regulatory compliance, supplier data collection, and supply chain risk assessment for QA, R&D, Regulatory, and Procurement teams at enterprise clients. The platform uses natural language processing to automate supplier data collection (citing high supplier response rates), monitors suppliers in real time against regulatory standards such as FDA, EU MRLs, California Prop 65, and PFAS, and applies AI-driven risk scoring to suppliers and facilities to streamline buyer-supplier collaboration. Otrafy is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website and product/contact pages but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Saul Ewing LLP
providers.description: Saul Ewing LLP is a U.S.-based law firm founded in 1921 as Saul, Ewing, Remick & Saul, with more than 450 attorneys across 17 U.S. offices spanning the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, Midwest, Florida, and California. The firm serves clients across 40+ industries with practice strengths in litigation, corporate and M&A, bankruptcy and restructuring, real estate, public finance, life sciences, financial services, intellectual property, labor and employment, and cybersecurity and privacy. Saul Ewing does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or machine-readable data product; its public technology surface is limited to its corporate website, a HighQ-powered client portal, the SEquel Alumni Portal at alumni.saul.com, employee remote-access tooling, and a small set of practice-specific blogs (Construction Industry Counselor, OZ and EB-5 Investments, Legacy Matters, The Friday Five). Two empty GitHub organizations (Saul-Ewing and saulewing) exist with zero public repositories.

providers.name: Ballard Spahr
providers.description: Ballard Spahr LLP is a national U.S. law firm founded in 1885 and headquartered in Philadelphia. Following its January 1, 2025 combination with Seattle-based Lane Powell, the firm operates as a "nationally recognized firm of more than 750 lawyers across 18 U.S. offices" with departments in Business and Transactions, Finance, Intellectual Property, Litigation, and Real Estate. The firm has historic depth in consumer financial services, real estate, public finance, and IP, and runs widely read thought-leadership properties including the Consumer Finance Monitor blog (with public RSS feed) and the Business Better podcast. Ballard Spahr does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI spec, or developer portal — its only machine-readable surface is the Consumer Finance Monitor RSS feed.

providers.name: Saris
providers.description: Saris (saris.ai) is an enterprise AI company building AI workflow agents for banks and credit unions. Its platform automates multi-step back-office processes across lending, compliance, and operations — document processing, data validation, core-system updates, and compliance tracking — while keeping humans in control with full audit trails. Saris integrates with financial-technology platforms such as Fiserv and with model providers including OpenAI and Anthropic, and is a recommended CCUA partner for Northeast credit unions. The company raised a $28.8M Series A and is backed by 8vc. As of this enrichment pass Saris exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Cambridge Blockchain
providers.description: Cambridge Blockchain, Inc. was a blockchain-based digital identity and compliance software company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Cambridge / Boston, Massachusetts. Its enterprise platform let financial institutions deliver strong digital identities to end users while meeting KYC/AML and data privacy obligations (including European GDPR), giving individuals control over their own personal identity data shared across institutions. The company was backed by investors including Partech and PayPal, and was acquired by Blockchains, Inc. in December 2020, after which its team and identity technology were folded into Blockchains' digital identity product. The former company website (cambridge-blockchain.com) is no longer served; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization and two first-party npm cryptographic libraries. No public HTTP API, OpenAPI specification, developer portal, or hosted documentation was ever published.

providers.name: DevSecOps
providers.description: Development, Security, and Operations methodology that integrates security practices within the DevOps process, emphasizing security automation and collaboration throughout the software development lifecycle. DevSecOps treats security as code, favors continuous monitoring and proactive testing, and delivers compliance and security capabilities as services consumable by development teams. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

providers.name: Fortu
providers.description: Fortu (Fortu Wealth Ltd) is a London-based fintech, founded in 2019, offering digital private banking for high-net-worth individuals and their businesses, including borderless multi-currency accounts, payments, and a curated selection of investment opportunities across fintech and real-estate-driven debt strategies. Fortu also operates a business-to-business Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) platform that lets private banks, wealth managers, and multi-family offices roll out their own branded investment and payments products, with automated payment processing and an API-driven compliance-monitoring tool. Co-founded by co-CEOs Firdavs Shakhidi and Azmat Sultanov, the company was selected for the 500 Global startup accelerator and raised an oversubscribed crowdfunding round (~GBP 500k) on Seedrs. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Fortu does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI, and its primary web deployment was offline (HTTP 402, disabled deployment) at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Fraugster
providers.description: Fraugster is a Berlin-based artificial intelligence company focused on payment fraud prevention and transaction risk scoring for online merchants, payment service providers, and acquirers. Its machine-learning platform was designed to analyze payments in real time to detect and block fraudulent transactions while reducing false declines and chargebacks. The company was surfaced through venture portfolio data (backed by Seedcamp) and added to the API Evangelist network. During this enrichment pass the company's public developer surface was not reachable to automated clients (the primary domain returns HTTP 403), so no API specifications, SDKs, or documentation could be harvested; only live infrastructure/domain-security signals were probed.

providers.name: HIPAA
providers.description: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) is U.S. legislation providing data privacy and security provisions for safeguarding medical information. HIPAA compliance is required for healthcare providers, health plans, and their business associates handling protected health information (PHI).

providers.name: LegalPad
providers.description: Legalpad (Legalpad Inc, Seattle) was a startup-focused US work-visa and immigration company founded by Todd Heine and Sara Itucas, who first began processing visas together at Teleborder (Y Combinator 2013) and reunited in Techstars Seattle in 2017. Legalpad paired software with staff immigration attorneys to file O-1, H-1B, L-1, TN, E-1/E-2, E-3 and B-1 work visas plus EB-1A, EB-1B, EB-1C, EB-2 and EB-2 NIW employment-based green cards, and said it had helped 500+ companies at roughly one-third the typical processing time. It raised a $2M seed in 2018 and a $10M Series A in 2020 before being acquired by Deel in 2022, after which it operated as "Legalpad by Deel" inside Deel Immigration. The legalpad.io web presence was retired after 2024 and the business now lives on as Deel Immigration. Legalpad never published a public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK or other developer surface, so there is no API artifact to enrich.

providers.name: LikeWise
providers.description: Likewise Software was a Bellevue, Washington enterprise software company building storage, identity and security products that bridged Linux, Unix and Mac systems into Microsoft Active Directory environments. Its OEM line, Likewise Storage Services, supplied SMB/CIFS multi-protocol file access to network storage vendors including HP StorageWorks, Riverbed, EMC Data Domain and NetApp, while Likewise Data Analytics and Governance covered auditing, reporting and compliance (HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, FISMA) over unstructured data. Its Likewise Enterprise and Likewise Open Active Directory integration products moved to BeyondTrust. Backed by Trinity Ventures, the company was acquired and no longer operates: there is no live website, developer portal, documentation or public API, and the likewise.com domain now redirects to an unrelated owner.

providers.name: Palerra
providers.description: Palerra, Inc. was a Santa Clara, California cloud security company whose LORIC platform delivered Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) capabilities: automated security monitoring, threat detection, configuration management, and compliance across SaaS and IaaS environments such as Salesforce, AWS, Microsoft Office 365, ServiceNow, and Box. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Wing Venture Capital, Palerra was acquired by Oracle in September 2016 and folded into the Oracle CASB Cloud Service. The palerra.com domain now redirects to Oracle's cloud security portal, and no independent public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification remains.

providers.name: Privacy by Design
providers.description: Privacy By Design is a framework and approach that embeds privacy protections into the design and operation of IT systems, networked infrastructure, and business practices from the ground up, rather than as an afterthought.

providers.name: Revv
providers.description: Revv (formerly RevvSales) is a document automation and electronic-signature platform that helps businesses prepare, automate, and execute business paperwork such as sales contracts, proposals, and agreements. The product offers 1,000+ customizable document templates, drag-and-drop editing, rule-based approval workflows, eSignatures with audit trails, real-time collaboration, and analytics, plus integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Sheets, and Zapier alongside a native REST API. Founded in India and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Revv was acquired by LegalZoom; its standalone developer and API-documentation subdomains (apidocs.revv.so, docs.revv.so, help.revv.so) now redirect into the LegalZoom application, so no independently documented Revv API specification is currently published.

providers.name: Stoke Talent
providers.description: Stoke Talent is a Freelance Management System (FMS) that lets enterprises source, onboard, manage, and pay external freelancers and contractors in one place while handling worker classification, contracts, tax, legal, and compliance. Founded in Israel and backed by Battery Ventures, Stoke was acquired by Fiverr in November 2021 for roughly $95M and subsequently rebranded as Fiverr Enterprise, now offered under the Fiverr Pro / Fiverr Enterprise product line. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or webhook documentation; this profile is maintained for network completeness.

providers.name: Tripwire
providers.description: Tripwire Inc. (part of Fortra), headquartered in Portland, Oregon, is an enterprise cybersecurity company known for file integrity monitoring (FIM), security configuration management (SCM), and vulnerability management. Its product line includes Tripwire Enterprise, the Tripwire Axon Agent, Tripwire IP360, Tripwire ExpertOps, and the original Open Source Tripwire. Tripwire's capabilities are delivered as on-premises and managed products with product-embedded REST APIs and configuration-management integrations (Puppet, Chef, Ansible) rather than a public developer portal; there is no public developer portal, public OpenAPI, or first-party client SDK on the public package registries as of this enrichment pass. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and is being enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: CUNA Mutual Group (TruStage)
providers.description: CUNA Mutual Group, now operating as TruStage, is an insurance and financial services company that provides insurance, retirement, and investment products to credit unions and their members. Founded in 1935 to serve the credit union movement, the company rebranded to TruStage in 2023, unifying its consumer-facing brands under a single identity. TruStage offers life insurance, auto and home insurance, AD&D, retirement planning, annuities, lending solutions, compliance services, and analytics tools to credit unions and their members.

providers.name: Huscarl
providers.description: Huscarl is an AI-native actuarial advisory firm focused on corporate self-insurance and captive insurance programs. The company provides actuarial intelligence and independent advisory for captive managers and owners, including feasibility studies for captive insurance entities, pricing and underwriting of uncommon risks with limited data, and reserve estimation and actuarial opinions. It helps large corporations determine whether they are paying the right amount for coverage and optimize their insurance strategy. Huscarl was founded by Alex Musy (CEO) and Paulien Jeunesse, who previously built cyber parametric insurance at Descartes Underwriting, and is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in San Francisco. As a professional-services actuarial firm it currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: LeapStack
providers.description: LeapStack (栈略数据 / Stack Strategy Data) is a Shanghai-based insurance technology and data-analytics company operating in China's health-insurance sector, applying big-data and risk-control intelligence to help insurers with claims, underwriting, and healthcare-cost analysis. It is a portfolio company of DCM Ventures and Qiming Venture Partners. Its public web presence (www.leapstack.tech) is a client-rendered marketing site; as of this enrichment pass no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or other public API surface was found. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Stable
providers.description: Stable is an insurtech company that provides price risk management and price insurance for agricultural and food commodities, helping farmers, food producers, buyers, and businesses hedge against the volatility of commodity prices. Backed by Anthemis and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub, Stable operates a price-stabilization platform rather than a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Wayco
providers.description: Wayco (Wayco AI, Inc.) is a Y Combinator (W26) startup building an AI operator for medical-legal cases. Its platform automates personal-injury and mass-tort case workflows end to end: AI voice agents answer and triage intake calls, match patients to medical providers by case type and location, coordinate telemedicine, summarize and analyze medical records at scale, and manage lead follow-up from first intake toward settlement. Founded by Iqbol Temirkhojaev and based in New York City, the company serves law firms, medical-billing, and insurance-claims teams. As of July 2026 Wayco is early stage and publishes a marketing site (wayco.ai) only, with no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable specifications yet.

providers.name: Willing
providers.description: Willing was an online estate-planning and will-making platform (a 500 Global portfolio company) that let consumers create wills, living wills, and related documents. The brand has since been absorbed into MetLife Legal Plans; as of this enrichment pass willing.com live-redirects (HTTP 302) to legalplans.com. Willing publishes no independent public API, developer portal, or GitHub organization of its own, so it carries no API artifacts beyond a domain-security probe of the surviving willing.com host.

providers.name: Adim
providers.description: Adim is an entertainment-technology and web3 media company co-founded in 2022 by It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney alongside Richard Rosenblatt, Chase Rosenblatt, Melissa Kaspers, and Spencer Marell. Adim invites a community of storytellers, writers, and fans to collaboratively create, develop, and co-own a new generation of intellectual property — stories, characters, and narrative universes known as the Adimverse — rewarding contributors with ownership stakes and a say in how the community is governed. The company raised a $5M seed round led by Chris Dixon of a16z crypto. Adim is a consumer creative platform rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Crosby
providers.description: Crosby is an agentic law firm that combines AI legal agents with barred attorneys to review commercial contracts in about an hour. Built for sales teams, it accelerates contract negotiation and time-to-signature with fixed, upfront per-document pricing, and integrates into existing workflows via Slack, email, and CLM/CRM triggers. Beyond contract review it offers business-specific knowledge agents and aggregated market data to improve negotiation outcomes. NYC-based, founded by Ryan Daniels and John Sarihan, and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Index Ventures, and Lux Capital. Crosby publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface as of this profiling.

providers.name: Dechert
providers.description: Dechert LLP is a global law firm founded in 1875 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, with "more than 900 lawyers" across 22 offices in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia (Wikipedia cites roughly 1,000 attorneys in 20 offices; the firm itself emphasizes a global footprint spanning the U.S., Europe, Asia, and the Middle East). The firm is known for market-leading practices in financial services and investment management, private equity, private credit, mergers and acquisitions, international arbitration, intellectual property, life sciences, white collar enforcement, and antitrust. Dechert publishes deep thought-leadership through its OnPoint series, Crypto Bytes, FSR Radar, THE CRED, and ReTorts; produces multiple podcasts (Dechert 4 Real, Committed Capital, Dechert On Reg); and operates proprietary information platforms including DAMITT (Dechert Antitrust Merger Investigation Timing Tracker), World Compass, World Passport, Dechert Direct, and a Box Portal. Despite these data-driven products, Dechert does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, GraphQL endpoint, webhook surface, status page, changelog, or developer portal, and does not publish an RSS feed for OnPoint or any blog series — its only public-facing subscription mechanism is an email preference form.

providers.name: Fenrock AI
providers.description: Fenrock AI is a Y Combinator (W26) company building specialized AI agents for the banking back office. Founded in 2026 and based in San Francisco by Charu Sharma and Michael M., Fenrock overlays on a bank's existing systems and ingests internal policies and standard operating procedures to automate compliance, financial-crime, and loan-operations workflows without requiring data migration. Its agents assist analysts with alert triage, case investigation, suspicious-activity-report (SAR) drafting, quality assurance, enhanced due diligence, KYC/KYB reviews, and sanctions/PEP monitoring, while preserving bullet-proof audit logs designed to pass regulatory examinations. Fenrock positions itself as an AI workspace that lets a single analyst process many times the volume of financial-crime and money-laundering cases. This profile is an API Evangelist network company record; Fenrock is an enterprise product company with no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Financial Regulation
providers.description: Financial regulation is the body of laws, rules, and supervisory frameworks governing financial markets, banks, broker-dealers, asset managers, payment providers, and crypto firms. Major regulators include the U.S. SEC, FINRA, CFTC, OCC, FRB, FDIC, FinCEN, CFPB; the UK FCA and PRA; the EU ESMA, EBA, and EIOPA; and global bodies like IOSCO and the Basel Committee. Core frameworks include MiFID II / MiFIR, Basel III, Dodd-Frank, Sarbanes-Oxley, EMIR, PSD2, GDPR, AML / KYC (FATF), and FATCA / CRS reporting.

providers.name: Leya
providers.description: Leya was a Stockholm-based legal AI startup founded in 2023 by Max Junestrand (CEO) and Sigge Labor, building an AI-powered workspace for law firms and legal professionals that automated repetitive document review, drafting, and legal research tasks across public sources and a firm's own private data. The company went through Y Combinator (Winter 2024 batch), partnered with leading Nordic firms such as Mannheimer Swartling beginning May 2023, raised a $10.5M seed (May 2024) and a $25M Series A (July 2024), and was named one of Stockholm's hottest startups by WIRED in 2024. Leya offered a collaborative legal AI workspace with tabular review (large-scale parallel document analysis) and was rolled out to 200+ law firms across 15+ countries under the Leya brand. On 19 February 2025 the company fully rebranded to Legora, retaining the same founders, Stockholm headquarters, and product, while expanding with agentic research tools and a Microsoft Word add-in. The Leya brand and product line have been entirely absorbed into Legora; there is no separate ongoing Leya product, no public developer API, no SDK, and no GitHub presence under the Leya name. This entry preserves the Leya identity for historical reference; see the legora entry for the ongoing company profile.

providers.name: Ritivel
providers.description: Ritivel is an AI-native regulatory and medical-writing platform for life sciences organizations, backed by Y Combinator (Winter 2026 batch). Its AI agents automate the drafting of regulatory submission documents such as Common Technical Documents (CTD), Clinical Study Reports (CSR), INDs, and BLAs, turning work that typically takes weeks into minutes. The platform generates comprehensive first drafts in Microsoft Word format that follow FDA and ICH requirements, with word-level traceability of every statement back to source documents, integrations with SharePoint, Veeva, and Outlook for document retrieval and follow-ups, a regulatory search over FDA and ICH guidelines, and a privacy posture built around local deployment with no cloud storage. It serves pharma, biotech, medtech, CROs, and CDMOs. Ritivel is an end-user application and does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Signify Group
providers.description: Signify Group is a London, United Kingdom-based ethical data science firm founded in 2017 by co-founder and CEO Jonathan Hirshler, applying machine learning, natural language understanding, and open-source intelligence (OSINT) to social and digital media data. Its flagship service, Threat Matrix, is widely regarded as the leading platform for detecting, analysing, evidencing, and actioning online abuse and fixated threats directed at athletes, clubs, leagues, player unions, federations, brands, and other public figures. Threat Matrix scans incoming public messages across X (Twitter), Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok in 39+ languages, uses "augmented intelligence" (AI speed combined with trained human analyst nuance) to triage racist, sexist, homophobic, anti-semitic, islamophobic, gambling-driven, and personally targeted abuse, and produces evidence-grade reports with network mapping that can be used by platforms, police, sponsors, and protection teams. Customers and partners include the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA), Kick It Out, the International Tennis Federation (ITF) and WTA Tour covering c.8,300 players, the International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS) protecting 1,000+ athletes and officials, the Badminton World Federation (BWF), the NCAA, and Japan's 2026 World Baseball Classic squad. Signify also operates ShareScore (media coverage and social buzz analytics), Sports Insights (fan engagement and athlete insight analytics), and Online Forensics (brand reputation, OSINT investigations, and risk assurance). Signify is a private services firm with no public developer API, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub organization; engagement is via direct sales and managed service contracts with rights-holders, leagues, federations, and enterprise clients.

providers.name: Secure Software Development Lifecycle
providers.description: A framework that integrates security practices into every phase of the software development process, from design and development through testing and deployment, to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities early. It is widely adopted across industries to safeguard digital assets and reduce security risks.

providers.name: &Volume
providers.description: &Volume is an AI-powered risk management platform for digital assets, built for institutional investors such as family offices, asset managers, and corporate treasuries. The platform normalizes data across exchanges, custodians, protocols, and strategies, then monitors risk in real time, compares uncorrelated yield and arbitrage opportunities, and rebalances capital among them with varying levels of AI-assisted automation. It connects to major exchanges (Binance, Coinbase), custody providers (Fireblocks, BitGo, Copper), protocols (Aave, Lido, Uniswap), and wallets (MetaMask, Ledger, Safe). Founded by a team drawn from Deutsche Bank, BNP Paribas, Jane Street, and EPAM, &Volume partners with the University of Edinburgh AI Laboratory and the LUMI supercomputer to build explainable, testable AI for capital orchestration as global assets move on-chain. Backed by 500 Global. No public API or developer program is published at this time.

providers.name: Aavenir
providers.description: Aavenir is an AI-powered contract lifecycle management (CLM) and source-to-pay software company that delivers procurement, legal, and finance workflow automation applications built natively on the ServiceNow platform. Its product suite includes Contractflow (contract lifecycle management), Obligationflow (contract obligation and compliance management), Sourcingflow (RFx and strategic sourcing), and Invoiceflow (accounts-payable invoice automation), using natural language processing and machine learning to digitize contracts, invoices, and procurement processes. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Alongside
providers.description: Alongside is an a16z-backed crypto company (alongside.xyz) founded in 2022. It originally launched the Alongside Crypto Market Index (AMKT), the first on-chain broad crypto market index token with a 0% annual fee, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, and Franklin Templeton. The company has since pivoted to AI-native compliance automation for scaling crypto firms, unifying fragmented KYC/AML/KYT tooling into a single system and reducing manual analyst burden for autonomous financial agents. As of this enrichment pass Alongside publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, MCP server, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity and probed domain security only.

providers.name: Alpharel
providers.description: Alpharel, Inc. was a Camarillo, California document-management and imaging company founded in 1981 that built turnkey digital document transmission and management systems (scanners, optical disks, terminals, LANs) for industrial, commercial, and government use. It acquired Optigraphics in 1993, renamed itself Altris Software in October 1996, and its business was ultimately succeeded by Spescom Software, Inc. of San Diego. Alpharel appears in the Battery Ventures portfolio list. The company is DEFUNCT under this name: it has no active first-party website, developer portal, API, or SDKs, so there is no API/developer surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: ArbiLex
providers.description: ArbiLex is a legal-fintech startup founded at the Harvard Innovation Labs in 2018 by Isabel Yang that brings AI and predictive analytics to high-stakes international arbitration and litigation finance. Its Bayesian machine learning and NLP models — trained on a dataset of over nine million cases — produce empirical, explainable case ratings that help counsel quantify uncertainty, reduce errors, and value claims. ArbiLex also operates the ArbiLex Funding Exchange (AFX), a data-driven marketplace pairing AI-rated cases with litigation-finance capital. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; no public developer API surface was found at time of enrichment.

providers.name: Aurigin Systems
providers.description: Aurigin Systems, Inc. was an intellectual-property management software company founded in 1992 and headquartered in Cupertino, California. It built online patent and trademark information services and business-automation software for intellectual-asset management, raising roughly $54M in venture funding (investors included Battery Ventures) over its lifetime. The company operated under Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection before substantially all of its assets were acquired by Information Holdings Inc. in May 2002. It is defunct, has no surviving website, developer portal, or public API, and was surfaced only as a historical portfolio lead from a Battery Ventures scrape.

providers.name: BetGenius
providers.description: BetGenius is the sportsbook-operator brand of Genius Sports, a London- and New York-listed sports data, technology, and commercial-services group. Founded in 2000 and operating as a Genius Sports business unit since the 2015 corporate consolidation, BetGenius provides licensed sportsbooks with an end-to-end B2B platform spanning official data and odds feeds, fully managed trading and risk management (Genius Trading Services), low-latency live video and interactive in-play streaming (BetVision and Genius Live Player), BetBuilder same-game-parlay pricing, ScoreCentre widgets, acquisition and retention marketing (FANHub, media buying, dynamic creative optimisation), and back-office sportsbook platform services (used by operators such as OPAP, 888, Betway, and Hard Rock Bet). Genius Sports sources official data from 400+ league partners — including the NFL, English Premier League, Serie A, EuroLeague, and PGA Tour — and serves 300+ licensed sportsbooks across regulated markets worldwide. BetGenius itself does not expose a self-service developer portal; its APIs (Booking API, Fixtures API v2, Matching API v2, Warehouse REST/Streaming/Publish APIs, LiveStats In-Arena and Licensing APIs, BetVision and Live Player integration SDKs) are documented at developer.geniussports.com and delivered to contracted operators via UAT and production environments using API-key authentication.

providers.name: CipherCloud
providers.description: CipherCloud was a cloud security company, founded in 2010, that pioneered the cloud access security broker (CASB) category. Its platform provided encryption and tokenization, data loss prevention, cloud discovery and shadow IT visibility, threat protection, and compliance controls for SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Office 365, ServiceNow, and Box. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Index Ventures among others, CipherCloud was acquired by mobile and cloud security vendor Lookout in early 2021, and its CASB technology was folded into Lookout's Secure Cloud Access offering. The standalone ciphercloud.com developer and product surface has since been retired; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical company record. No live public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or documentation surface could be located during enrichment (ciphercloud.com returns HTTP 404 and no developer/docs subdomains resolve).

providers.name: Conjectag
providers.description: Conjectag (Conject AG / Conject Holding GmbH) was a Munich-based German construction technology company founded in 2000 that provided cloud-based software for the built environment, covering project management, collaboration, document control, and construction cost management for the AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) sector. It was surfaced as a historical Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company. Conject was acquired by the Australian construction collaboration platform Aconex in March 2016, and Aconex was subsequently acquired by Oracle in December 2017; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live website or developer/API surface. This profile is retained for network provenance rather than active enrichment.

providers.name: Court Buddy
providers.description: Court Buddy is a legal services marketplace that connected consumers and small businesses with independent attorneys for flat-fee, on-demand legal help, aiming to make legal representation more affordable and accessible. It operated under the LawChamps brand (lawchamps.com) and was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable surface was found during enrichment, and the primary web property is currently unreachable.

providers.name: Dasera
providers.description: Dasera is a data security company in the data security posture management (DSPM) and data governance space, founded by Ani Chaudhuri and backed by Sierra Ventures. Its platform was built to continuously discover, classify, and monitor sensitive data across cloud and on-premises data stores (databases, warehouses, data lakes) and to surface data security, privacy, and compliance risk across the data lifecycle. As of this enrichment pass the standalone dasera.com origin is unreachable (a Cloudflare 1001 origin error with a failed TLS handshake), so no live developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI surface could be harvested; this profile records the domain-security posture that could still be probed via DNS/TLS and remains a stub awaiting a live API surface.
